1	# Reference lock
2	
3	**Load in Step 1b, for every tier.** Refero's research-first method, adapted to this
4	skill's four-tier gate (`SKILL.md` Step 2): Tier 0 locked · Tier 1 derive · Tier 2
5	reference · Tier 3 invent. The lock is not a Tier-2-only artifact — every tier states
6	one before Step 2 runs, because every tier is a claim about where the direction comes
7	from, and an unstated claim is how Tier 1 gets skipped in favour of invention.
8	
9	| | |
10	|---|---|
11	| **Reads** | The brief, Step 1 pre-flight findings, Step 2 tier evidence (`DESIGN.md`, brand assets, user URL/screenshot, or nothing), the design catalog, 21st.dev for tech/SaaS shots, Refero MCP when configured. |
12	| **Does** | Runs the research loop below, captures references as read images (never from memory), fills the reference-lock block and decision ledger, checks the build against anti-averaging and token/media-role preservation. |
13	| **Writes** | Nothing persisted by default — the lock is stated in-session, out loud, before Step 2 and Step 4. When the system is being locked to a portable file, its fields feed [`design-md.md`](design-md.md). |
14	| **Human checks** | Whether the named primary reference is actually the dominant voice in the build, not a label pasted over an averaged result — the one judgment this file cannot automate. |
15	
16	---
17	
18	## What changes per tier
19	
20	The loop is identical; only what plays the role of "the reference" changes.
21	
22	- **Tier 0 — locked.** Reconstructed, not invented: read `DESIGN.md` and what's
23	  already built from it, and write down what "preserve" means. Primary = the
24	  locked system itself.
25	- **Tier 1 — derive.** Primary = the brand evidence (logo, wordmark, hex, deployed
26	  site, `tailwind.config` colours). Borrowed details may come from competitor or
27	  category references; they extend the language, never re-set it.
28	- **Tier 2 — reference.** Primary = the user-supplied URL or screenshot. Refero's
29	  native case; the fields map straight across.
30	- **Tier 3 — invent.** Primary = the invented world's own bible
31	  ([`invention.md`](invention.md)) — locking against it stops the second component
32	  from drifting into a different invented world than the first.
33	
34	At every tier, a major visual choice with no source in the lock is not shipped.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## A brief is not a build target
39	
40	Refero states the rule this file exists to enforce, in one sentence: *"**A brief is not a
41	build target.** Before implementation, lock either a user-provided visual source, an
42	existing product/design-system target, a selected generated mockup, or an explicit
43	reference-locked direction approved for direct build."*
44	
45	This is the sentence that closes the skip route. When the direction feels obvious and the
46	signature act is being built straight from the brief, the visual target still gets named
47	first — one line saying what this is being built *toward* and what must not drift:
48	
49	```text
50	Build target: [existing UI / user screenshot / URL capture / selected mockup / approved reference lock]
51	What must not drift: [canvas, typography, accent roles, layout, media, density]
52	```
53	
54	If no target exists and the visual direction is material, explore options or get one
55	reference-locked direction approved. A build whose only stated source is the brief is a
56	build with no source at all.
57	
58	## Research loop
59	
60	Six angles, not one query:
61	
62	1. **Broad aesthetic** — the mood in plain language ("warm coastal Nordic hospitality").
63	2. **Domain / category** — what this business actually is.
64	3. **Known brand** — a specific strong player in the segment, named.
65	4. **Register** — the row from `SKILL.md`'s register table this brief lands in.
66	5. **Anti-reference** — one thing this build should *not* look like, sharpening the
67	   boundary the same way a rejected direction does in the lock block below.
68	6. **Cross-domain wildcard** — one reference from *outside* the category, chosen for a
69	   quality rather than a subject. *"A banking app can be inspired by a meditation app's
70	   calm."* Upstream's map:
71	
72	   | This brief's domain | Look at |
73	   |---|---|
74	   | Healthcare | Meditation apps (calm), fitness apps (motivation), journaling (reflection) |
75	   | Finance | Productivity tools (clarity), weather apps (data viz), news apps (hierarchy) |
76	   | Education | Games (engagement), music apps (progression), social apps (community) |
77	   | E-commerce | Editorial sites (storytelling), gallery apps (browsing), travel (discovery) |
78	   | Enterprise | Consumer apps (polish), design tools (power + clarity), docs (wayfinding) |
79	
80	   *"Don't force connections — but don't limit yourself to competitors either."* Competitors
81	   solve the same problem the same way, which is precisely how a category default becomes
82	   invisible. `select.py --wildcard` is the catalogue-side version of this angle.
83	
84	**Quality over quantity: *"5 excellent references beat 20 mediocre ones."*** A wall of
85	screenshots is not research; it is deferred judgment. Curate down before capturing.
86	
87	Then: **capture 3–4 full references as images and read them**, long pages in
88	viewport-sized slices. Memory returns wrong facts — two market-leading pages
89	turned out to *centre* their heroes, and one coloured words inside the headline
90	instead of switching typeface, opposite of what was assumed before the images
91	were opened.
92	
93	**Every captured reference carries two lines, not one:**
94	
95	```text
96	What to take: [the specific element or quality to learn from]
97	What to leave: [what does not apply here]
98	```
99	
100	*"This prevents wholesale copying."* A reference with no lesson is decoration, and a
101	reference with only a "take" line is the one that quietly becomes the whole build. The
102	"leave" line is also what makes the primary/borrowed split below enforceable rather than
103	declarative.
104	
105	**Extract more than colour and type.** From each reference, read out: layout system,
106	section rhythm and composition · card, button and surface treatments · borders, shadows,
107	radius · elevation and depth rules · imagery, graphic and illustration treatment · media
108	asset strategy (real asset, generated, code-native primitive, product screenshot, or
109	placeholder) · do and don't rules · **one memorable visual move to adapt**. A lock that
110	carries a palette and a typeface and nothing structural is why a build "referenced" a page
111	it looks nothing like.
112	
113	**Give each source a bounded job.** *"Primary style: overall mood, density, and structure.
114	Secondary styles: specific borrowed details. User context: adapt everything to the product,
115	audience, and task."* A source with no job is a source that gets averaged.
116	
117	From the 3–4 captured, pick **one primary** and take **1–2 borrowed details** from
118	the rest. Nothing else survives into the lock.
119	
120	**Flag accessibility failures in the references themselves.** *"A beautiful reference with
121	2:1 contrast ratios is not inspiration — it's a cautionary tale."* Name it when you capture
122	it, so the trait does not travel into the lock as craft.
123	
124	### Sources, in order
125	
126	1. **The design catalog** — `~/anti-slop-design/design-catalogue/`,
127	   `python scripts/query.py --family … --register … --grammar …`. Query by the
128	   register named in `SKILL.md`'s table, not by vibe.
129	2. **User-supplied URL or screenshot** — Tier 2's native input; also valid at any
130	   tier as a borrowed-detail source.
131	3. **21st.dev** for tech/SaaS product shots — browse, screenshot, study the
132	   treatment; borrow the principle and rebuild it in the locked tokens, never paste
133	   a component with its own palette into a Tier 0–2 build.
134	4. **Refero MCP**, if configured — `refero_search_styles` → `refero_get_style`.
135	   Optional. State plainly when it is not configured rather than silently skipping
136	   it; do not treat its absence as license to skip the research loop itself.
137	
138	### When the results are weak
139	
140	Sparse or generic results are a query problem before they are a source problem. Climb this
141	ladder before concluding the catalogue has nothing (Refero `mcp-tools.md` § If Results Are
142	Weak):
143	
144	1. **Broaden the query.**
145	2. **Remove extra adjectives or constraints.** Two adjectives and a register is usually one
146	   adjective too many.
147	3. **Search adjacent categories.**
148	4. **Try a known-product or best-brand query.** Name a specific strong player instead of
149	   describing a type.
150	5. **Inspect later pages.** The first page of any index is the most averaged part of it.
151	
152	Only after all five is "no usable reference in this register" a finding — and then it is
153	stated in the lock, not silently converted into invention.
154	
155	### Transcribe the category's live headlines
156	
157	Before writing a word of copy, read the **five best live pages in the category and quote
158	their headlines verbatim** into the lock. *"The bar is what the reader has already seen, not
159	what sounds nice in isolation"* (`upstream/slopmonster/references/sources.md`). Five lines,
160	copied exactly, with the source named. They belong here rather than in
161	[`copy-gate.md`](copy-gate.md) because they are a *reference* capture: the same discipline
162	as the four screenshots, applied to language, and read before the copy pass rather than
163	during it.
164	
165	## The reference-lock block
166	
167	Verbatim fields, filled before any code:
168	
169	```text
170	Primary reference/direction: [one dominant source, named]
171	Preserve: [3-5 traits that must survive: canvas, type, accent, layout, density, media]
172	Borrow only: [1-2 specific secondary details]
173	Role rules: [source token/component meanings to preserve — CTA-only, code-only, decorative-only]
174	Media strategy: [photo:unsplash | photo:pexels | product surface | drawn system | generated | placeholder]
175	Reject: [defaults/averages that would collapse the direction]
176	Token commitments: [canvas, type, accent, radius, border/shadow, imagery — each with its role]
177	```
178	
179	**Media strategy is an enum, not prose.** Pick exactly one value per media slot so
180	drift is visible at a glance: a hero declared `photo:unsplash` that quietly becomes
181	a CSS gradient is a caught regression; a hero declared "some kind of photo" is not.
182	
183	## Decision ledger
184	
185	Every entry in the lock traces back through this table:
186	
187	| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
188	|---|---|---|---|
189	| [palette / type / layout / media choice] | [reference / catalog query / brand asset / craft rule] | [token or component role to preserve] | [reason specific to this brief] |
190	| **Memorable detail** | [the reference the move was adapted from] | [what the move does on this page] | [why *this* brief earns it] |
191	
192	**A major visual choice with no row here is not shipped.** Not "shipped and
193	justified after" — the row exists before the choice does.
194	
195	**The `Memorable detail` row is mandatory, and the rule applies to it too.** Refero's
196	requirement is unambiguous: *"Create at least one memorable detail: a visual move,
197	interaction, layout choice, or copy detail users would remember."* No row, not shipped —
198	including for the signature act itself, which is the row most often left blank on the
199	grounds that it is obvious. An example of a filled row from upstream's own worked case:
200	*"Memorable detail | 'Operational value' strip showing saved hours/cost by plan | Brief +
201	analytics product context | Metric strip as evidence, not decoration | Makes pricing feel
202	tied to outcome."*
203	
204	## The asset lock
205	
206	Written **before** anyone starts searching or generating — Step 5b has a pipeline but no
207	spec upstream of it, and an asset sourced without a spec is an asset chosen by whatever the
208	search returned. One block per media slot:
209	
210	```text
211	Asset role: [hero image / texture / illustration / thumbnail / cutout]
212	Slot: [dimensions / aspect ratio / location on the page]
213	Art direction: [source, palette, subject, rendering, crop, density]
214	Avoid: [wrong palette, extra text, brand drift, generic placeholders]
215	```
216	
217	The `Avoid` line is the one that earns its keep: it is the reject field applied to a single
218	asset, and it is what a QA pass compares the delivered frame against.
219	*"Generated assets must be placed into the implementation before handoff or documented as
220	blocked"* — never quietly downgraded to a gradient. That downgrade is the media-role drift
221	this file's next section already bans, caught one step earlier.
222	
223	---
224	
225	## Anti-averaging
226	
227	Choose a dominant direction. Secondary references contribute narrow, named details;
228	they do not get to soften the primary one. The failure mode is specific: a dark
229	workbench reference, an acid-yellow document site, and a serif editorial page do not
230	average into a warm cream canvas with muted clay accents — **dark + acid + serif is
231	not cream + orange + polite serif.** Dark → cream, saturated → muted clay, sharp →
232	rounded, distinctive layout → generic hero-and-sections: each swap is the
233	intersection eating the direction, not synthesis.
234	
235	Run these against the lock before shipping — ported from `anti-ai-slop.md`:
236	
237	- **Identity test.** If the first viewport could belong to any other company,
238	  branding lost to averaging. Add the one detail that makes this unmistakably *this*
239	  brand's build.
240	- **Editorial test.** If swapping the logo for a coffee shop, boutique hotel, or
241	  literary magazine still makes the hero feel plausible, the build has drifted into
242	  generic calm-editorial slop regardless of what the lock says on paper.
243	- **Screenshot test.** Would this pass next to real products in the named
244	  register, or does it read as the safe middle every other page also landed on?
245	
246	A lock that names a dominant primary and still fails these three was averaged during
247	implementation, not during research — check the built page against the lock's
248	"Reject" line specifically.
249	
250	## Token-role and media-role preservation
251	
252	**Token-role preservation.** A source's role for a colour, radius, shadow, or
253	component is part of the token, not separable from it. A CTA-only accent used as a
254	section background, a code-only syntax colour promoted to UI chrome, or a decorative
255	gradient turned into a core surface are all role drift. Preserve the role or drop
256	the token — never repurpose it to make a layout "work."
257	
258	**Media-role preservation.** An image-led reference never collapses to text-only
259	because the image was hard to produce. If the real asset genuinely is not
260	available, the placeholder must be honest, not silent:
261	
262	```text
263	Placeholder — [slot name]
264	Aspect: [ratio, e.g. 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile]
265	Art direction: [subject, lighting, crop the real asset will match]
266	Alt: [describes the intended real subject, not "placeholder image"]
267	```
268	
269	A placeholder with no aspect ratio, no art direction, and generic alt text is the
270	same failure as no image at all — it just fails one render cycle later.
271	
272	---
273	
274	## Three persona sketches
275	
276	`SKILL.md` Step 5 pass 12 and [`verbs/review.md`](verbs/review.md) § 4 both resolve ties
277	with "named personas". Nothing in the chain created any, so the tie-break pointed at an
278	artifact that did not exist. It does now, and it is three lines in `BRIEF.md` — not the
279	per-project persona documents upstream files away, which is a research deliverable this
280	chain has no room for.
281	
282	Select and write **three**, following upstream's proportions (*"2–3 primary users, 1–2 edge
283	case users, 1 stress case user"*), compressed to one line each:
284	
285	```text
286	Primary: [who they are] · [device and connection] · [what they came to do]
287	Edge:    [who sits at the margin] · [the ability or context that puts them there] · [what breaks first]
288	Stress:  [the same job under a named difficult circumstance] · [what they cannot afford to lose]
289	```
290	
291	**The conditions are situational, not only permanent.** Upstream's spectrum is explicit that
292	*"bright sunlight, noisy environment, one hand occupied, driving, multitasking, emotional
293	distress, unfamiliar language, slow connection"* belong beside vision, hearing, motor and
294	cognitive conditions. A stress persona on a Swedish harbour-restaurant page is a person on a
295	phone, outdoors, in sun, deciding where to eat in the next ten minutes — and that persona
296	decides more layout questions than any abstract one.
297	
298	**Write the intersections down.** *"A sighted user in bright sunlight has similar needs to a
299	low-vision user. A stressed parent holding a baby has similar motor constraints to someone
300	with limited hand mobility. A non-native speaker has similar needs to someone with a
301	cognitive processing difference."* Each intersection is a universal-design opportunity: one
302	fix that pays twice.
303	
304	**Then ask the one question that makes the set honest:** *"Which persona makes you most
305	uncomfortable?"* — *"that one probably needs the most attention."* Ask it of the brief, and
306	of the user when there is a user to ask. Discomfort is the signal that a persona was
307	included for completeness and is about to be designed around rather than for.
308	
309	Sketches that read as cardboard cutouts have failed. The check is upstream's own: *"do these
310	feel like real people, or cardboard cutouts?"*
311	
312	## Feeding Step 2 and Step 5
313	
314	**Into Step 2.** At **Tier 2**, the lock *is* the direction — its primary reference
315	sets the token commitments directly. At **Tiers 0–1**, the lock is the **quality
316	bar** the locked or derived system has to clear: the locked tokens still win on
317	value, but the captured references are what "as good as" means, concretely.
318	
319	**Into Step 5 visual QA.** Carry the lock's fields straight into the QA pass:
320	
321	```text
322	Source truth: [the reference lock, or the DESIGN.md it fed]
323	Implementation evidence: [local screenshot, deployed URL screenshot, captured app state]
324	Viewport/state: [desktop/mobile, route, theme, interaction state]
325	```
326	
327	Classify findings P0–P3 (broken/unreadable · major drift from the lock · moderate
328	mismatch or missing state · post-handoff polish). **No handoff with an open P0, P1,
329	or P2.** A P3 may ship with the finding named; P0–P2 block.
330	
331	## Worked example — Skärgårdskrogen (Swedish harbour restaurant, warm photographic)
332	
333	A harbourside restaurant on the Bohuslän coast. Register: **warm photographic**
334	(`SKILL.md` register table — harbour restaurant, guesthouse, tourism, family
335	business), with `klova/` as this skill's own in-repo worked example for the
336	register (`house-physics.md`).
337	
338	**Research loop:**
339	
340	1. Broad aesthetic — "warm coastal Nordic hospitality."
341	2. Domain/category — harbourside seafood dining, Bohuslän archipelago.
342	3. Known brand — a west-coast Swedish harbour restaurant with a photograph-led site.
343	4. Register — warm photographic, per the table above; cross-check against `klova/`.
344	5. Anti-reference — the editorial-print register (`calyx.html`): its apparatus on a
345	   family harbour restaurant reads as pretension, not craft.
346	
347	Four captured and read: `klova/` itself, two competitor harbour-restaurant sites,
348	and `calyx.html` as the anti-reference boundary check.
349	
350	**Reference-lock block:**
351

# Reference lock

**Load in Step 1b, for every tier.** Refero's research-first method, adapted to this
skill's four-tier gate (`SKILL.md` Step 2): Tier 0 locked · Tier 1 derive · Tier 2
reference · Tier 3 invent. The lock is not a Tier-2-only artifact — every tier states
one before Step 2 runs, because every tier is a claim about where the direction comes
from, and an unstated claim is how Tier 1 gets skipped in favour of invention.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | The brief, Step 1 pre-flight findings, Step 2 tier evidence (`DESIGN.md`, brand assets, user URL/screenshot, or nothing), the design catalog, 21st.dev for tech/SaaS shots, Refero MCP when configured. |
| **Does** | Runs the research loop below, captures references as read images (never from memory), fills the reference-lock block and decision ledger, checks the build against anti-averaging and token/media-role preservation. |
| **Writes** | Nothing persisted by default — the lock is stated in-session, out loud, before Step 2 and Step 4. When the system is being locked to a portable file, its fields feed [`design-md.md`](design-md.md). |
| **Human checks** | Whether the named primary reference is actually the dominant voice in the build, not a label pasted over an averaged result — the one judgment this file cannot automate. |

---

## What changes per tier

The loop is identical; only what plays the role of "the reference" changes.

- **Tier 0 — locked.** Reconstructed, not invented: read `DESIGN.md` and what's
  already built from it, and write down what "preserve" means. Primary = the
  locked system itself.
- **Tier 1 — derive.** Primary = the brand evidence (logo, wordmark, hex, deployed
  site, `tailwind.config` colours). Borrowed details may come from competitor or
  category references; they extend the language, never re-set it.
- **Tier 2 — reference.** Primary = the user-supplied URL or screenshot. Refero's
  native case; the fields map straight across.
- **Tier 3 — invent.** Primary = the invented world's own bible
  ([`invention.md`](invention.md)) — locking against it stops the second component
  from drifting into a different invented world than the first.

At every tier, a major visual choice with no source in the lock is not shipped.

---

## A brief is not a build target

Refero states the rule this file exists to enforce, in one sentence: *"**A brief is not a
build target.** Before implementation, lock either a user-provided visual source, an
existing product/design-system target, a selected generated mockup, or an explicit
reference-locked direction approved for direct build."*

This is the sentence that closes the skip route. When the direction feels obvious and the
signature act is being built straight from the brief, the visual target still gets named
first — one line saying what this is being built *toward* and what must not drift:

```text
Build target: [existing UI / user screenshot / URL capture / selected mockup / approved reference lock]
What must not drift: [canvas, typography, accent roles, layout, media, density]
```

If no target exists and the visual direction is material, explore options or get one
reference-locked direction approved. A build whose only stated source is the brief is a
build with no source at all.

## Research loop

Six angles, not one query:

1. **Broad aesthetic** — the mood in plain language ("warm coastal Nordic hospitality").
2. **Domain / category** — what this business actually is.
3. **Known brand** — a specific strong player in the segment, named.
4. **Register** — the row from `SKILL.md`'s register table this brief lands in.
5. **Anti-reference** — one thing this build should *not* look like, sharpening the
   boundary the same way a rejected direction does in the lock block below.
6. **Cross-domain wildcard** — one reference from *outside* the category, chosen for a
   quality rather than a subject. *"A banking app can be inspired by a meditation app's
   calm."* Upstream's map:

   | This brief's domain | Look at |
   |---|---|
   | Healthcare | Meditation apps (calm), fitness apps (motivation), journaling (reflection) |
   | Finance | Productivity tools (clarity), weather apps (data viz), news apps (hierarchy) |
   | Education | Games (engagement), music apps (progression), social apps (community) |
   | E-commerce | Editorial sites (storytelling), gallery apps (browsing), travel (discovery) |
   | Enterprise | Consumer apps (polish), design tools (power + clarity), docs (wayfinding) |

   *"Don't force connections — but don't limit yourself to competitors either."* Competitors
   solve the same problem the same way, which is precisely how a category default becomes
   invisible. `select.py --wildcard` is the catalogue-side version of this angle.

**Quality over quantity: *"5 excellent references beat 20 mediocre ones."*** A wall of
screenshots is not research; it is deferred judgment. Curate down before capturing.

Then: **capture 3–4 full references as images and read them**, long pages in
viewport-sized slices. Memory returns wrong facts — two market-leading pages
turned out to *centre* their heroes, and one coloured words inside the headline
instead of switching typeface, opposite of what was assumed before the images
were opened.

**Every captured reference carries two lines, not one:**

```text
What to take: [the specific element or quality to learn from]
What to leave: [what does not apply here]
```

*"This prevents wholesale copying."* A reference with no lesson is decoration, and a
reference with only a "take" line is the one that quietly becomes the whole build. The
"leave" line is also what makes the primary/borrowed split below enforceable rather than
declarative.

**Extract more than colour and type.** From each reference, read out: layout system,
section rhythm and composition · card, button and surface treatments · borders, shadows,
radius · elevation and depth rules · imagery, graphic and illustration treatment · media
asset strategy (real asset, generated, code-native primitive, product screenshot, or
placeholder) · do and don't rules · **one memorable visual move to adapt**. A lock that
carries a palette and a typeface and nothing structural is why a build "referenced" a page
it looks nothing like.

**Give each source a bounded job.** *"Primary style: overall mood, density, and structure.
Secondary styles: specific borrowed details. User context: adapt everything to the product,
audience, and task."* A source with no job is a source that gets averaged.

From the 3–4 captured, pick **one primary** and take **1–2 borrowed details** from
the rest. Nothing else survives into the lock.

**Flag accessibility failures in the references themselves.** *"A beautiful reference with
2:1 contrast ratios is not inspiration — it's a cautionary tale."* Name it when you capture
it, so the trait does not travel into the lock as craft.

### Sources, in order

1. **The design catalog** — `~/anti-slop-design/design-catalogue/`,
   `python scripts/query.py --family … --register … --grammar …`. Query by the
   register named in `SKILL.md`'s table, not by vibe.
2. **User-supplied URL or screenshot** — Tier 2's native input; also valid at any
   tier as a borrowed-detail source.
3. **21st.dev** for tech/SaaS product shots — browse, screenshot, study the
   treatment; borrow the principle and rebuild it in the locked tokens, never paste
   a component with its own palette into a Tier 0–2 build.
4. **Refero MCP**, if configured — `refero_search_styles` → `refero_get_style`.
   Optional. State plainly when it is not configured rather than silently skipping
   it; do not treat its absence as license to skip the research loop itself.

### When the results are weak

Sparse or generic results are a query problem before they are a source problem. Climb this
ladder before concluding the catalogue has nothing (Refero `mcp-tools.md` § If Results Are
Weak):

1. **Broaden the query.**
2. **Remove extra adjectives or constraints.** Two adjectives and a register is usually one
   adjective too many.
3. **Search adjacent categories.**
4. **Try a known-product or best-brand query.** Name a specific strong player instead of
   describing a type.
5. **Inspect later pages.** The first page of any index is the most averaged part of it.

Only after all five is "no usable reference in this register" a finding — and then it is
stated in the lock, not silently converted into invention.

### Transcribe the category's live headlines

Before writing a word of copy, read the **five best live pages in the category and quote
their headlines verbatim** into the lock. *"The bar is what the reader has already seen, not
what sounds nice in isolation"* (`upstream/slopmonster/references/sources.md`). Five lines,
copied exactly, with the source named. They belong here rather than in
[`copy-gate.md`](copy-gate.md) because they are a *reference* capture: the same discipline
as the four screenshots, applied to language, and read before the copy pass rather than
during it.

## The reference-lock block

Verbatim fields, filled before any code:

```text
Primary reference/direction: [one dominant source, named]
Preserve: [3-5 traits that must survive: canvas, type, accent, layout, density, media]
Borrow only: [1-2 specific secondary details]
Role rules: [source token/component meanings to preserve — CTA-only, code-only, decorative-only]
Media strategy: [photo:unsplash | photo:pexels | product surface | drawn system | generated | placeholder]
Reject: [defaults/averages that would collapse the direction]
Token commitments: [canvas, type, accent, radius, border/shadow, imagery — each with its role]
```

**Media strategy is an enum, not prose.** Pick exactly one value per media slot so
drift is visible at a glance: a hero declared `photo:unsplash` that quietly becomes
a CSS gradient is a caught regression; a hero declared "some kind of photo" is not.

## Decision ledger

Every entry in the lock traces back through this table:

| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| [palette / type / layout / media choice] | [reference / catalog query / brand asset / craft rule] | [token or component role to preserve] | [reason specific to this brief] |
| **Memorable detail** | [the reference the move was adapted from] | [what the move does on this page] | [why *this* brief earns it] |

**A major visual choice with no row here is not shipped.** Not "shipped and
justified after" — the row exists before the choice does.

**The `Memorable detail` row is mandatory, and the rule applies to it too.** Refero's
requirement is unambiguous: *"Create at least one memorable detail: a visual move,
interaction, layout choice, or copy detail users would remember."* No row, not shipped —
including for the signature act itself, which is the row most often left blank on the
grounds that it is obvious. An example of a filled row from upstream's own worked case:
*"Memorable detail | 'Operational value' strip showing saved hours/cost by plan | Brief +
analytics product context | Metric strip as evidence, not decoration | Makes pricing feel
tied to outcome."*

## The asset lock

Written **before** anyone starts searching or generating — Step 5b has a pipeline but no
spec upstream of it, and an asset sourced without a spec is an asset chosen by whatever the
search returned. One block per media slot:

```text
Asset role: [hero image / texture / illustration / thumbnail / cutout]
Slot: [dimensions / aspect ratio / location on the page]
Art direction: [source, palette, subject, rendering, crop, density]
Avoid: [wrong palette, extra text, brand drift, generic placeholders]
```

The `Avoid` line is the one that earns its keep: it is the reject field applied to a single
asset, and it is what a QA pass compares the delivered frame against.
*"Generated assets must be placed into the implementation before handoff or documented as
blocked"* — never quietly downgraded to a gradient. That downgrade is the media-role drift
this file's next section already bans, caught one step earlier.

---

## Anti-averaging

Choose a dominant direction. Secondary references contribute narrow, named details;
they do not get to soften the primary one. The failure mode is specific: a dark
workbench reference, an acid-yellow document site, and a serif editorial page do not
average into a warm cream canvas with muted clay accents — **dark + acid + serif is
not cream + orange + polite serif.** Dark → cream, saturated → muted clay, sharp →
rounded, distinctive layout → generic hero-and-sections: each swap is the
intersection eating the direction, not synthesis.

Run these against the lock before shipping — ported from `anti-ai-slop.md`:

- **Identity test.** If the first viewport could belong to any other company,
  branding lost to averaging. Add the one detail that makes this unmistakably *this*
  brand's build.
- **Editorial test.** If swapping the logo for a coffee shop, boutique hotel, or
  literary magazine still makes the hero feel plausible, the build has drifted into
  generic calm-editorial slop regardless of what the lock says on paper.
- **Screenshot test.** Would this pass next to real products in the named
  register, or does it read as the safe middle every other page also landed on?

A lock that names a dominant primary and still fails these three was averaged during
implementation, not during research — check the built page against the lock's
"Reject" line specifically.

## Token-role and media-role preservation

**Token-role preservation.** A source's role for a colour, radius, shadow, or
component is part of the token, not separable from it. A CTA-only accent used as a
section background, a code-only syntax colour promoted to UI chrome, or a decorative
gradient turned into a core surface are all role drift. Preserve the role or drop
the token — never repurpose it to make a layout "work."

**Media-role preservation.** An image-led reference never collapses to text-only
because the image was hard to produce. If the real asset genuinely is not
available, the placeholder must be honest, not silent:

```text
Placeholder — [slot name]
Aspect: [ratio, e.g. 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile]
Art direction: [subject, lighting, crop the real asset will match]
Alt: [describes the intended real subject, not "placeholder image"]
```

A placeholder with no aspect ratio, no art direction, and generic alt text is the
same failure as no image at all — it just fails one render cycle later.

---

## Three persona sketches

`SKILL.md` Step 5 pass 12 and [`verbs/review.md`](verbs/review.md) § 4 both resolve ties
with "named personas". Nothing in the chain created any, so the tie-break pointed at an
artifact that did not exist. It does now, and it is three lines in `BRIEF.md` — not the
per-project persona documents upstream files away, which is a research deliverable this
chain has no room for.

Select and write **three**, following upstream's proportions (*"2–3 primary users, 1–2 edge
case users, 1 stress case user"*), compressed to one line each:

```text
Primary: [who they are] · [device and connection] · [what they came to do]
Edge:    [who sits at the margin] · [the ability or context that puts them there] · [what breaks first]
Stress:  [the same job under a named difficult circumstance] · [what they cannot afford to lose]
```

**The conditions are situational, not only permanent.** Upstream's spectrum is explicit that
*"bright sunlight, noisy environment, one hand occupied, driving, multitasking, emotional
distress, unfamiliar language, slow connection"* belong beside vision, hearing, motor and
cognitive conditions. A stress persona on a Swedish harbour-restaurant page is a person on a
phone, outdoors, in sun, deciding where to eat in the next ten minutes — and that persona
decides more layout questions than any abstract one.

**Write the intersections down.** *"A sighted user in bright sunlight has similar needs to a
low-vision user. A stressed parent holding a baby has similar motor constraints to someone
with limited hand mobility. A non-native speaker has similar needs to someone with a
cognitive processing difference."* Each intersection is a universal-design opportunity: one
fix that pays twice.

**Then ask the one question that makes the set honest:** *"Which persona makes you most
uncomfortable?"* — *"that one probably needs the most attention."* Ask it of the brief, and
of the user when there is a user to ask. Discomfort is the signal that a persona was
included for completeness and is about to be designed around rather than for.

Sketches that read as cardboard cutouts have failed. The check is upstream's own: *"do these
feel like real people, or cardboard cutouts?"*

## Feeding Step 2 and Step 5

**Into Step 2.** At **Tier 2**, the lock *is* the direction — its primary reference
sets the token commitments directly. At **Tiers 0–1**, the lock is the **quality
bar** the locked or derived system has to clear: the locked tokens still win on
value, but the captured references are what "as good as" means, concretely.

**Into Step 5 visual QA.** Carry the lock's fields straight into the QA pass:

```text
Source truth: [the reference lock, or the DESIGN.md it fed]
Implementation evidence: [local screenshot, deployed URL screenshot, captured app state]
Viewport/state: [desktop/mobile, route, theme, interaction state]
```

Classify findings P0–P3 (broken/unreadable · major drift from the lock · moderate
mismatch or missing state · post-handoff polish). **No handoff with an open P0, P1,
or P2.** A P3 may ship with the finding named; P0–P2 block.

## Worked example — Skärgårdskrogen (Swedish harbour restaurant, warm photographic)

A harbourside restaurant on the Bohuslän coast. Register: **warm photographic**
(`SKILL.md` register table — harbour restaurant, guesthouse, tourism, family
business), with `klova/` as this skill's own in-repo worked example for the
register (`house-physics.md`).

**Research loop:**

1. Broad aesthetic — "warm coastal Nordic hospitality."
2. Domain/category — harbourside seafood dining, Bohuslän archipelago.
3. Known brand — a west-coast Swedish harbour restaurant with a photograph-led site.
4. Register — warm photographic, per the table above; cross-check against `klova/`.
5. Anti-reference — the editorial-print register (`calyx.html`): its apparatus on a
   family harbour restaurant reads as pretension, not craft.

Four captured and read: `klova/` itself, two competitor harbour-restaurant sites,
and `calyx.html` as the anti-reference boundary check.

**Reference-lock block:**

```text
Primary reference/direction: klova/ — centred logo lockup over full-bleed harbour photography, no rail, no kicker, no edition marker.
Preserve: centred logo lockup with no rail; full-bleed hero photograph with generous framing air on secondary images; one real outlined button sized to be pressed; warm serif display at conversational (not oversized-drop-cap) scale; dark-navy footer as the page's one tonal inversion.
Borrow only: dotted carousel indicator for the food gallery (competitor B — klova/ has no gallery, so this is a genuinely new need, not a style import); 12px rounded image corners (competitor B).
Role rules: the outlined button is CTA-only, never a secondary link style; the navy footer tone is inversion-only, never a section background elsewhere on the page.
Media strategy: photo:unsplash, sourced and vendored per photo-sources.md until real restaurant photography is supplied; hero 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile, framed with 24-48px air — never full-bleed-with-type-over, the editorial-print move this build explicitly rejects.
Reject: kicker microformat, grain film, ledger pricing, edition markers, italic serif drop caps — all editorial-print apparatus a family harbour restaurant cannot plausibly publish.
Token commitments: warm ivory canvas; near-black ink; one terracotta accent used only on the button and one wordmark word (never as fill); slate captions with a separate, measured value for the dark footer ground.
```

**Decision ledger:**

| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warm photographic, not editorial print | `SKILL.md` register table + anti-reference read of `calyx.html` | register selects apparatus | Family-run harbour restaurant, not a publishing entity |
| Centred logo lockup, no rail | `klova/` (primary) | layout role: identity-first hero | The photograph is the primary hire, not editorial structure |
| Real outlined button | `klova/` (primary) | CTA-only | Warm-photographic register expects a pressable button, unlike print/cinematic typeset links |
| Dotted carousel for gallery | Competitor B (borrowed) | gallery navigation only | `klova/` had no gallery; licensed as one named borrowed detail, not a wholesale style import |
| One terracotta accent, display-scale only | `house-physics.md` structural rule | accent role: CTA + display, never fill | Prevents the accent diluting into a second colour system |

A rejected direction here would average `klova/`'s warm photographic register with
`calyx.html`'s editorial apparatus into a soft-cream page with a restrained kicker
and a half-outlined button that is neither a typeset link nor a real one — the
dark+acid+serif-vs-cream+orange+polite-serif failure, in miniature.

## Two additions from the 2026-09-03 A/B run (AB05)

- **A colour-swapped word in a headline is a gate-89 signal even without a serif.** "Se *exakt* vad som ändrades" with *exakt* in the accent is the same reflex as the italic word swap; use it only when a locked reference does it and the word carries the claim.
- **Token commitments name the anatomy of every priced or listed surface.** Write `pricing: ledger (hairline rows, display numerals)` or `features: label-rail`, so the lock carries house physics into Step 4 instead of falling back to bordered cards.

1	# Motion smoothness — why a page that renders correctly can still look cheap
2	
3	Anton, r7 (FEEDBACK.md F-012): *"scrolleffekten renderade som den skulle, men det såg
4	hackigt och billigt gjort ut."* The measured answer is F-013. Read this before writing
5	any scroll-driven motion, and read it again before "fixing" motion that someone has
6	called janky — because **two different faults produce that same sentence**, and the cure
7	for one does nothing for the other.
8	
9	## The two faults
10	
11	| | The value steps | The page drops frames |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| What you see | Motion advances in visible notches | Motion stutters and lags the hand |
14	| What the clock says | 60 fps, nothing wrong | frame p95 well over 20 ms |
15	| Where it comes from | A raw scroll value written 1:1 | Too much work per frame |
16	| What fixes it | Damp the value (`--sc-ps`) | Cut the work (`performance.md`) |
17	
18	Measure both before changing anything: `scripts/motion_probe.py` reports frame time and
19	value continuity in one run. Guessing which fault you have is how a session spends an
20	afternoon smoothing something that was never stepping.
21	
22	## Fault 1 — the raw value
23	
24	`scrollcraft.js` damps exactly two things: the video playhead (lerp 0.18, deadband,
25	seek coalescing) and the pointer devices `tilt` / `magnet`. Its own docstring explains
26	why: *"wheel events do not arrive at a constant rate and a 1:1 write reproduces every
27	gap in them."*
28	
29	That reasoning is right, and the engine does not apply it to `--sc-p`. Everything
30	`read()` writes — `--sc-p` itself, cue opacity, parallax, pan, kinetic units,
31	`clip-path`, drift — is written 1:1 from raw scroll position, on the scroll event
32	behind a one-frame rAF guard. On a mouse wheel the value stands still between notches
33	and then jumps.
34	
35	Two things make it worse:
36	
37	- **`--sc-p` is an unregistered custom property.** To CSS it is a string, so it never
38	  interpolates, and no `@property` registration exists anywhere in the engine.
39	- **`scrollcraft.css` sets `transition: none`** on `[data-sc-cue]` and `[data-sc-copy]`
40	  once `.sc-ready` lands. That is deliberate — JS owns the value — but it means nothing
41	  bridges the gap between two writes.
42	
43	**F-011 did not cause this.** `var reduce = false` turned the playhead lerp *on*
44	(rate 1.0 → 0.18). `reduce` gates ten sites in the engine and every one is a disable
45	branch. The stepping is architectural and predates the override.
46	
47	### The rule
48	
49	> **Bespoke motion reads `--sc-ps`, never raw `--sc-p`, whenever it drives something the
50	> eye sees move** — `transform`, `object-position`, `clip-path`, `mask-position`,
51	> `background-position`. Cue opacity may read `--sc-p`.
52	
53	`--sc-ps` is published by `scripts/scroll/sc-smooth.js`, copied in beside the engine and
54	loaded after it. The engine is never edited (`scroll/NOTE.md`: copy, never edit). The
55	shim lerps at 0.16 per frame with a 0.0005 deadband, registers `--sc-ps` as a real
56	`<number>` so CSS can interpolate it, stops its own rAF loop when nothing is moving, and
57	sets `will-change` **only while an act is actually in motion** — correcting the engine
58	CSS's seven class-level promotions, which `motion.md` § Bans forbids.
59	
60	A page's own rAF painters (`paintHeroPool`, `paintMotion`, a word scrub) read `--sc-ps`
61	too. `?preview=` modes set `window.__scFreezeMotion = true`, and the shim then tracks the
62	raw value exactly so a screenshot shows the formed state, not a lerp in flight.
63	
64	Measured, same motion, same wheel cadence (`tests/motion/`):
65	
66	| | frame p95 | staircase | largest single-frame step |
67	|---|---|---|---|
68	| `staircase.html` (raw `--sc-p` → `rotateY`) | 16.7 ms | 18 | 5.6 % |
69	| `smooth.html` (lerped) | 16.7 ms | **0** | **1.4 %** |
70	
71	The frame clock is identical in both. The difference is entirely in the value.
72	
73	## Fault 2 — the page is genuinely slow
74	
75	Damping a value on a page that cannot hold 60 fps just makes a smooth curve arrive late.
76	V3b, measured 2026-09-08 with no CPU throttling at all: frame p95 49.9 ms, 62 frames over
77	33 ms, 4.9 MB transferred, 19 font files, 17 long tasks during scroll, four elements with
78	a resting `will-change`. See `performance.md` for the budget and `scripts/perf_probe.py`
79	for the measurement.
80	
81	## Pace — the third thing people call "not smooth"
82	
83	From upstream scroll-craft's `worldflight.md` § 7c, the only place in the corpus where
84	someone diagnosed the complaint to root cause: *"Two separate faults get described as

# Motion smoothness — why a page that renders correctly can still look cheap

Anton, r7 (FEEDBACK.md F-012): *"scrolleffekten renderade som den skulle, men det såg
hackigt och billigt gjort ut."* The measured answer is F-013. Read this before writing
any scroll-driven motion, and read it again before "fixing" motion that someone has
called janky — because **two different faults produce that same sentence**, and the cure
for one does nothing for the other.

## The two faults

| | The value steps | The page drops frames |
|---|---|---|
| What you see | Motion advances in visible notches | Motion stutters and lags the hand |
| What the clock says | 60 fps, nothing wrong | frame p95 well over 20 ms |
| Where it comes from | A raw scroll value written 1:1 | Too much work per frame |
| What fixes it | Damp the value (`--sc-ps`) | Cut the work (`performance.md`) |

Measure both before changing anything: `scripts/motion_probe.py` reports frame time and
value continuity in one run. Guessing which fault you have is how a session spends an
afternoon smoothing something that was never stepping.

## Fault 1 — the raw value

`scrollcraft.js` damps exactly two things: the video playhead (lerp 0.18, deadband,
seek coalescing) and the pointer devices `tilt` / `magnet`. Its own docstring explains
why: *"wheel events do not arrive at a constant rate and a 1:1 write reproduces every
gap in them."*

That reasoning is right, and the engine does not apply it to `--sc-p`. Everything
`read()` writes — `--sc-p` itself, cue opacity, parallax, pan, kinetic units,
`clip-path`, drift — is written 1:1 from raw scroll position, on the scroll event
behind a one-frame rAF guard. On a mouse wheel the value stands still between notches
and then jumps.

Two things make it worse:

- **`--sc-p` is an unregistered custom property.** To CSS it is a string, so it never
  interpolates, and no `@property` registration exists anywhere in the engine.
- **`scrollcraft.css` sets `transition: none`** on `[data-sc-cue]` and `[data-sc-copy]`
  once `.sc-ready` lands. That is deliberate — JS owns the value — but it means nothing
  bridges the gap between two writes.

**F-011 did not cause this.** `var reduce = false` turned the playhead lerp *on*
(rate 1.0 → 0.18). `reduce` gates ten sites in the engine and every one is a disable
branch. The stepping is architectural and predates the override.

### The rule

> **Bespoke motion reads `--sc-ps`, never raw `--sc-p`, whenever it drives something the
> eye sees move** — `transform`, `object-position`, `clip-path`, `mask-position`,
> `background-position`. Cue opacity may read `--sc-p`.

`--sc-ps` is published by `scripts/scroll/sc-smooth.js`, copied in beside the engine and
loaded after it. The engine is never edited (`scroll/NOTE.md`: copy, never edit). The
shim lerps at 0.16 per frame with a 0.0005 deadband, registers `--sc-ps` as a real
`<number>` so CSS can interpolate it, stops its own rAF loop when nothing is moving, and
sets `will-change` **only while an act is actually in motion** — correcting the engine
CSS's seven class-level promotions, which `motion.md` § Bans forbids.

A page's own rAF painters (`paintHeroPool`, `paintMotion`, a word scrub) read `--sc-ps`
too. `?preview=` modes set `window.__scFreezeMotion = true`, and the shim then tracks the
raw value exactly so a screenshot shows the formed state, not a lerp in flight.

Measured, same motion, same wheel cadence (`tests/motion/`):

| | frame p95 | staircase | largest single-frame step |
|---|---|---|---|
| `staircase.html` (raw `--sc-p` → `rotateY`) | 16.7 ms | 18 | 5.6 % |
| `smooth.html` (lerped) | 16.7 ms | **0** | **1.4 %** |

The frame clock is identical in both. The difference is entirely in the value.

## Fault 2 — the page is genuinely slow

Damping a value on a page that cannot hold 60 fps just makes a smooth curve arrive late.
V3b, measured 2026-09-08 with no CPU throttling at all: frame p95 49.9 ms, 62 frames over
33 ms, 4.9 MB transferred, 19 font files, 17 long tasks during scroll, four elements with
a resting `will-change`. See `performance.md` for the budget and `scripts/perf_probe.py`
for the measurement.

## Pace — the third thing people call "not smooth"

From upstream scroll-craft's `worldflight.md` § 7c, the only place in the corpus where
someone diagnosed the complaint to root cause: *"Two separate faults get described as
'it doesn't feel smooth', and only one of them is smoothing."*

- **Inconsistent pace is the worse one.** Across a multi-act or multi-leg sequence,
  `rate = weight / seconds` must hold within a few percent. On the `orrery` build it
  varied 36 % across ten legs and the owner's word for it was "not smooth"; evened to
  6 %, the same footage read as one continuous move.
- **Too fast reads as cheap.** For a fly-through, 0.21–0.22 vh per second of film is the
  floor. The per-8-seconds guardrail is a dead-scroll floor, not a taste target.
- **Damping and weights fix different halves.** *"The damping is what removes wheel
  judder; the weights are what remove the surging."* For a worldflight use
  `data-sc-lerp` **0.12**, not the 0.18 default, and widen `data-sc-seam` to ~0.16.

`motion_probe.py` reports `max_step` per act, so an act that surges relative to its
neighbours shows up as a spread across runs rather than as a feeling. Full port, with
the weight arithmetic and the worldflight knob values: [`scroll/pace.md`](scroll/pace.md).

## The bar

A signature act is not finished until, at 4× CPU throttling:

- `staircase = 0`
- `max_step ≤ 3 %` of the value's own range
- frame p95 ≤ 20 ms, zero frames over 33 ms
- both scroll directions measured, not just downward

## What the harness still cannot tell you

Upstream's `verify.md` says it plainly: *"Whether the motion is smooth. Contiguous frames
prove the clip advances; they do not prove it advances evenly."* `motion_probe.py` closes
most of that gap and does not close all of it. Watch the contact sheet for a move that
lurches, reverses, or stalls in the middle, and watch the sparkline the probe writes: a
curve with a flat shoulder is an act that stops dead mid-travel, which no single number
reports.

One known, accepted inconsistency: `scripts/scroll/scrollcraft.css` line 98 still carries
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { html { scroll-behavior: auto } }`. It only
disables smooth anchor jumping and touches no act, and the engine is never edited, so it
stays — documented here rather than silently tolerated.

## Related

[`scroll/devices.md`](scroll/devices.md) · [`scroll/pace.md`](scroll/pace.md) ·
[`performance.md`](performance.md) ·
[`motion.md`](motion.md) · `scripts/motion_probe.py` · `scripts/scroll/sc-smooth.js` ·
FEEDBACK.md F-011, F-012, F-013.

1	# The device kit, condensed
2	
3	Nine ways scroll can drive the page. Pick per beat, never per page: ≥4 device
4	families, never the same one twice running. Every act publishes `--sc-p` (0–1)
5	on itself, so bespoke CSS can ride the same value the kit devices use. Full
6	depth, worked examples, and every trap: `upstream/scroll-craft/.../references/devices.md`.
7	
8	| # | Device | Syntax | Span / rate | One-line rule |
9	|---|---|---|---|---|
10	| 1 | `scrub` | `data-sc-act="scrub" data-sc-span="2.6" data-sc-dwell="0.35"` on the section; `data-sc-scrub data-sc-src="…"` on the `<video>` | span 2.2–3.0 for a hero | ≤2 per page. The wheel scrubs a pre-rendered clip; spend it on the open |
11	| 2 | `pin` | `data-sc-act="pin" data-sc-span="3"` | span ≥1.2 (below that, progress jumps 0→1 in one notch) | The frame holds, copy states cross over inside it |
12	| 3 | `pan` | `data-sc-act="pan" data-sc-span="3.2"`; rail gets `data-sc-pan="0.08"` | ~1vh per item + 1 | Lateral = breadth, not hierarchy. Overflow must be measured, not assumed |
13	| 4 | `reveal` | `data-sc-reveal="up|down|left|right|iris" data-sc-reveal-at="0.15 0.55"` | — | `clip-path` wipe = change of state. `iris` once per page at most |
14	| 5 | `kinetic` | `data-sc-kinetic="lines|words|chars"` on a cued heading | — | Lines almost always right, chars ~never. One kinetic headline per act |
15	| 6 | `parallax` | `data-sc-parallax="-0.6"` | rate is **hundreds of px total travel**, not a fraction — usable range 0.3–1.5 (framed), 1–2 (full-bleed) | Never on body copy. 3 layers is plenty |
16	| 7 | `count` | `data-sc-count="0 4,200" data-sc-count-at="0.1 0.5"` | 1.2–1.8s outside an act (`data-sc-count-ms`) | Only real numbers. No verified figure, no counter |
17	| 8 | `flow` + `in` | `data-sc-in data-sc-stagger="70"` on the wrap | stagger 30–80ms | The rest of the page. Fires once, opacity+14px rise, ~620ms ease-out |
18	| 9 | pointer: `tilt` / `magnet` / `spotlight` | `data-sc-tilt="7"` (5–9°), `data-sc-magnet="0.28"` (0.2–0.35, CTA only), `data-sc-spotlight` (publishes `--sc-mx`/`--sc-my`) | — | Gated to `(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`. Never gated on reduced motion (F-011, superseded 2026-09-07) |
19	
20	`drift` (`data-sc-drift="#0A0806"` on an act) is not a device, it's a
21	property: the page ground interpolates toward it while the act is live. 3–5
22	stops, one theme family. On a page of many *short* acts several can be
23	part-way through at once — paint grounds per section instead of drifting; see
24	upstream §10.
25	
26	## The cue contract — what verification actually catches you on
27	
28	`data-sc-cue="from [to [rampIn [rampOut]]]"`, all in act progress 0–1.
29	
30	| Form | Behaviour |
31	|---|---|
32	| `"0.2"` | fades in at 0.2, **holds to the end of the act** |
33	| `"0.1 0.6"` | in, plateau, out (ramps default 30% of window each) |
34	| `"0 0.78 0"` | **greet**: full opacity at act start, then fades — the hero form |
35	| `"0 1 0 0"` | **greet and hold**: full at p=0, no ramp either end |
36	
37	**The plateau is the point.** Without one, a cue is a triangle that touches full
38	opacity for a single instant, so the reader has to stop on exactly the right
39	pixel to see the line at full strength and every heading reads slightly faded.
40	`"0.1 0.9 0.15 0.4"` — fast in, long slow out — is the confident form. Cue
41	windows on a pinned act **overlap by design**, roughly 15% of the act: the
42	outgoing line is still fading while the next arrives, and a gap between cues
43	reads as a loading failure.
44	
45	Five rules, each one a real bug this fixture has caught:
46	
47	- **A hero cue needs the greet form.** A plain `"0 0.7"` means the first
48	  screen every visitor sees has no headline on it.
49	- **The last act's cue must hold** (one value). A two-value close cue fades
50	  the CTA out before the page ends.
51	- **Only the last act may hold.** A one-value cue on a *middle* pinned act
52	  stays lit through the whole un-pin slide — the line travels a full viewport
53	  up, crosses fixed chrome, overlaps the next section. Invisible until
54	  measured; shows up as a contrast failure nobody meant.
55	- **Ground or greet.** A pinned stage is fully visible ~1vh *before* its own
56	  progress leaves 0. A plain two-value first cue shows an empty stage for
57	  that whole travel — give the act a ground (image/colour already doing
58	  work) or open with a greet cue.
59	- **Clip time ≠ cue time.** A `scrub` clip is mapped across the stage's
60	  *entire visible life* (default), not across the pinned travel, because the
61	  stage is on screen for a viewport before the pin starts and after it ends.
62	  Cues keep using `p` (they belong to the pin); the clip uses a separately
63	  computed `vp`. Reaching for `data-sc-clip-map="travel"` reintroduces the
64	  freeze — there's almost no reason to.
65	
66	Two more that a harness will not catch by itself:
67	
68	- **Pan overflow must be measured, not assumed.** The rail travels exactly
69	  `scrollWidth - viewport`; a rail narrower than the viewport travels **zero**
70	  and the act reads as a still. `rail.scrollWidth - innerWidth` — check it,
71	  don't guess.
72	- **Parallax rate is hundreds of pixels total, not a viewport fraction** — see
73	  the table above. A rate of 0.35 across three viewport-heights of scroll is
74	  35px: invisible.
75	
76	Composing an act: devices stack (a pinned stage can hold a scrub clip, a
77	parallax layer, a kinetic headline, a spotlight at once), but one thing is the
78	reason the act exists — say that thing in one sentence or the act has none.
79	
80	## The playhead is lerped (§1)
81	
82	The mechanism the whole kit's smoothness rests on, and the one F-012 kept
83	being blamed on. **Scroll never writes `currentTime`.** It writes a *target*,
84	and a standalone rAF loop walks the clip toward that target at a fixed
85	fraction per frame:
86	
87	> *"Wheel events do not arrive at a constant rate, so a 1:1 write reproduces
88	> every gap in them and the clip reads as a stutter rather than a glide."*
89	
90	Three mechanisms, all on by default:
91	
92	- **Lerp 0.18 per frame.** `data-sc-lerp` overrides it, on the mount root for
93	  the whole page or on a single `<video>`. **Clamped to 0.02–1 and never read
94	  as 0** — a 0 lerp is a playhead that never moves. Reach for an override only
95	  when a page's clips are short enough that 0.18 visibly lags the hand.
96	  Worldflight wants 0.12 instead; see [`pace.md`](pace.md).
97	- **Deadband: 8 ms desktop, 20 ms mobile.** A write smaller than that costs a
98	  seek and shows nothing; on a phone it costs more than it shows.
99	- **Seek coalescing.** No seek is queued while the decoder is still resolving
100	  the last one. *"A fast flick otherwise piles seeks up and freezes the clip."*
101	
102	An offscreen clip that has already reached its target stops being touched at
103	all. (Upstream states the offscreen skip without a threshold value; the 0.002
104	figure belongs to `shoot.mjs`'s settle test, below, not to this skip.)
105	
106	This applies to **every** scrub clip on the page, act or worldflight. It is
107	also why the shooter waits for the playhead to arrive before each frame:
108	
109	> *"A frame captured mid-lerp is a frame the page never actually holds."*
110	
111	`shoot.mjs` settles on `|current − target| < 0.002 && !seeking`. Any harness
112	the chain runs against a scrubbed page inherits that requirement — a
113	screenshot taken mid-lerp makes the run unrepeatable, not merely imprecise.
114	
115	Upstream also drops the damping to 1.0 (no smoothing at all) under reduced
116	motion. **That branch does not port: F-011.** The lerp is unconditional here,
117	which is the correct behaviour anyway — it is a smoothing mechanism, not an
118	effect, and turning it off is what produces the stepping fault.
119	
120	## Layered scenes: where the premium feel comes from (§6)
121	
122	Ported from `devices.md` § 6, measured off a reference premium site and proven
123	on a live build. A flat page moves as one sheet; a layered page is a stack of
124	cut-out planes sliding past each other, and *"the eye reads that differential
125	motion as depth before it reads anything else."* It is the single biggest
126	difference between a page that feels built and one that feels assembled, and
127	it costs three transparent images and a multiplier each.
128	
129	- **Plan the planes back to front.** Far ridge, mid ridge, the product, then a
130	  **foreground plane in front of the product**. The product sits between mid
131	  and front, so the foreground overtakes it as the reader scrolls. That
132	  overtaking is the move.
133	- **Small rate differences, not big ones.** The reference hero lags the far
134	  plane **31%** behind the page, the mid plane **17%**, the product **20%**,
135	  and foreground and copy travel at exactly **1×**. Adjacent planes differ by
136	  **10–30%**. Larger stops reading as distance and starts reading as things
137	  sliding around. **Copy always rides at 1×.**
138	- **Shape the foreground for the product.** A straight-edged foreground covers
139	  the product's CTA within a few hundred pixels of scroll. Cut it so it dips
140	  where the product is and rises at the edges, and the button stays in view
141	  two to three times as long.
142	- **Every plane is solid below its silhouette.** Cut-out art that fades to
143	  transparent at the bottom lets the plane behind show through as the planes
144	  separate. Fill each column solid from its first opaque pixel down.
145	- **Fade the section floor.** Planes travel past the section's bottom edge and
146	  are clipped there. A gradient to the page ground over the last 200–300 px,
147	  layered above every plane, hides the clip line at any scroll position.
148	
149	Three traps, each of which cost a round of fixes:
150	
151	- A global `img { max-width: 100% }` shrinks an absolutely positioned plane to
152	  the viewport on phones, so the far layer never shows. **Planes carry
153	  `max-width: none` and a fixed pixel width.**
154	- **Never `transition: transform` on a parallaxed element.** A reveal class is
155	  the usual culprit. The transition eases every per-frame scroll write over
156	  its own duration, and on a phone that reads as the product lagging a full
157	  second behind the thumb. Parallaxed elements transition **opacity only**.
158	- Replacing a plane's art under the same filename ships nothing to a phone
159	  holding the old bytes. **New art gets a new name.**
160	
161	`data-sc-parallax` and a raw scroll multiplier are the same tool in different
162	units. What matters is the **ratio between planes**, not the absolute travel.
163	
164	## The premium fade-in, exactly (§8)
165	
166	The `flow` + `in` device is most of the page, so its defaults decide how the
167	page feels between the acts:
168	
169	| Ingredient | Value |
170	|---|---|
171	| Opacity | 0 → 1 |
172	| Rise | **~14 px** |
173	| Duration | **~620 ms**, ease-out |
174	| Stagger | **30–80 ms**, children in reading order |
175	| Trigger | IntersectionObserver, `-12%` bottom root margin, **fires once** |
176	
177	- **A fade with no rise reads as a loading glitch.** A rise **past 24 px reads
178	  as a slide.** 14 px is the band, not a starting point to tune upward.
179	- The `-12%` margin fires the reveal when the reader is looking, not when the
180	  first pixel clears the fold.
181	- `data-sc-in` is what the engine watches. Without it nothing fires and the
182	  stagger children stay hidden.
183	- **Content that re-hides on the way back up is a defect, not an effect.**
184	- *"Larger, slower, or bouncier is never more premium; the restraint is the
185	  signal."*
186	
187	**A flow section directly after a pinned act takes reduced padding.** The
188	pinned stage needs a full viewport to scroll off, and full `--sc-section`
189	padding on top of that delays the flow section's first content by another
190	screen. The harness will not call it dead scroll — correctly, the stage is
191	moving — and the reader still sees a near-empty screen. Cut the block padding
192	there and start the first reveal near `p = 0`.
193	
194	## Rail settle on `pan` (§3)
195	
196	Lateral travel alone reads as a slideshow on rails. **Give the rail's items a
197	staggered settle driven from `--sc-p`** and they read as a drawer being
198	pulled instead.
199	
200	- **Exempt the first item** — a `pan` act needs its opening content already
201	  present.
202	- **Floor the opacity around 0.55**, so a not-yet-settled card reads as
203	  arriving rather than as failing to load.
204	
205	Upstream gates the settle to `prefers-reduced-motion` — **utgår, F-011**.
206	The settle always runs. What *does* survive from
207	the same passage is the reachability requirement, which is not a motion
208	preference at all: a `pan` rail's transform **is** the navigation, so nothing
209	may zero it and park the act on its first screenful. Every item in a rail
210	stays reachable, and that is checked on the sheet, not assumed.
211	
212	Two more, from the same section:
213	
214	- **Card copy is read while cropped.** Items enter and leave through the
215	  viewport edges, so a heading is half-shown for most of its life, and two
216	  half-headings side by side can read as a third word (`TRACE` beside
217	  `EVALUATE` becoming `RE EVALUATE`). Keep card headings to one or two short
218	  words and expect every line to be read partially cut off.
219	- If three items do not reach half a viewport of overflow, **the fix is more
220	  rail, not wider cards**: put the act's heading in as the first item and a
221	  closing note as the last. Both earn their place, and they add the width the
222	  travel needs.
223	
224	## Devices that cannot share an element (§9)
225	
226	**`magnet`, `parallax` and `cue` all write `transform`.** The magnet writes
227	every frame in its own rAF loop, so it silently wins and the cue's entrance
228	rise is discarded — a visible animation lost to a race, with nothing in the
229	console.
230	
231	- On a magnetic CTA, set **`data-sc-rise="0"`** so the cue writes a no-op
232	  instead of losing to the magnet.
233	- A cued element that wants its own continuous transform drives an **inner
234	  wrapper** from `--sc-p` in CSS, rather than stacking a second device on the
235	  same node.
236	
237	All three pointer devices **interpolate toward** the pointer rather than
238	tracking it directly: *"direct tracking reads as artificial because it carries
239	no momentum."* They stay gated to `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` so
240	touch never fires a false hover — that gate is a pointer-capability query, not
241	a motion preference, and it stands.
242	The reduced-motion half of the same sentence does not port (F-011).
243	
244	## Kinetic type: the mask and the re-split (§5)
245	
246	Each unit slides up from **behind a mask**, so it enters from a clean edge
247	rather than simply fading.
248	
249	- **Line masks must reserve room for descenders.** A mask clipped to the line
250	  box shears the tails off g, y, p and j, *"and that is the single most common
251	  way this effect looks broken."*
252	- **Line splitting measures real line boxes, so it re-runs after
253	  `document.fonts.ready`.** Do not call it on text still loading its face. The
254	  same `fonts.ready` handle earns its place twice over: a webfont swapping in
255	  changes the measured height of every copy block, so anything sized against
256	  those blocks (a scrim plate, a rail) is wrong until it re-measures.
257	- Lines are almost always right; words for a short punch line; characters
258	  approximately never, *"because it turns reading into waiting."*
259	- **One kinetic headline per act, at most.**
260	
261	## What makes a `count` land (§7)
262	
263	- **Ease out, hard.** A cubic ease-out, so most of the distance goes by in the
264	  first third and the last digits settle slowly. *"A linear count reads as a
265	  slot machine."*
266	- **1.2–1.8 s.** Under a second and the reader misses that it moved; past two
267	  and they are waiting for a number they have already guessed.
268	- **Fires at half visibility, once**, so the reader is looking at it when it
269	  starts, and it never re-runs on the way back up.
270	- **Pair it with the fade.** A counter inside a `data-sc-in` stack rises in
271	  with its label and starts ticking as it arrives — *"the same numbers static
272	  on the page read as a spreadsheet."*
273	- Write the target exactly as it should render, commas included; the engine
274	  strips them before parsing and applies `tabular-nums` so the layout does not
275	  jitter.
276
