# The device kit, condensed

Nine ways scroll can drive the page. Pick per beat, never per page: ≥4 device
families, never the same one twice running. Every act publishes `--sc-p` (0–1)
on itself, so bespoke CSS can ride the same value the kit devices use. Full
depth, worked examples, and every trap: `upstream/scroll-craft/.../references/devices.md`.

| # | Device | Syntax | Span / rate | One-line rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scrub` | `data-sc-act="scrub" data-sc-span="2.6" data-sc-dwell="0.35"` on the section; `data-sc-scrub data-sc-src="…"` on the `<video>` | span 2.2–3.0 for a hero | ≤2 per page. The wheel scrubs a pre-rendered clip; spend it on the open |
| 2 | `pin` | `data-sc-act="pin" data-sc-span="3"` | span ≥1.2 (below that, progress jumps 0→1 in one notch) | The frame holds, copy states cross over inside it |
| 3 | `pan` | `data-sc-act="pan" data-sc-span="3.2"`; rail gets `data-sc-pan="0.08"` | ~1vh per item + 1 | Lateral = breadth, not hierarchy. Overflow must be measured, not assumed |
| 4 | `reveal` | `data-sc-reveal="up|down|left|right|iris" data-sc-reveal-at="0.15 0.55"` | — | `clip-path` wipe = change of state. `iris` once per page at most |
| 5 | `kinetic` | `data-sc-kinetic="lines|words|chars"` on a cued heading | — | Lines almost always right, chars ~never. One kinetic headline per act |
| 6 | `parallax` | `data-sc-parallax="-0.6"` | rate is **hundreds of px total travel**, not a fraction — usable range 0.3–1.5 (framed), 1–2 (full-bleed) | Never on body copy. 3 layers is plenty |
| 7 | `count` | `data-sc-count="0 4,200" data-sc-count-at="0.1 0.5"` | 1.2–1.8s outside an act (`data-sc-count-ms`) | Only real numbers. No verified figure, no counter |
| 8 | `flow` + `in` | `data-sc-in data-sc-stagger="70"` on the wrap | stagger 30–80ms | The rest of the page. Fires once, opacity+14px rise, ~620ms ease-out |
| 9 | pointer: `tilt` / `magnet` / `spotlight` | `data-sc-tilt="7"` (5–9°), `data-sc-magnet="0.28"` (0.2–0.35, CTA only), `data-sc-spotlight` (publishes `--sc-mx`/`--sc-my`) | — | Gated to `(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`. Never gated on reduced motion (F-011, superseded 2026-09-07) |

`drift` (`data-sc-drift="#0A0806"` on an act) is not a device, it's a
property: the page ground interpolates toward it while the act is live. 3–5
stops, one theme family. On a page of many *short* acts several can be
part-way through at once — paint grounds per section instead of drifting; see
upstream §10.

## The cue contract — what verification actually catches you on

`data-sc-cue="from [to [rampIn [rampOut]]]"`, all in act progress 0–1.

| Form | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `"0.2"` | fades in at 0.2, **holds to the end of the act** |
| `"0.1 0.6"` | in, plateau, out (ramps default 30% of window each) |
| `"0 0.78 0"` | **greet**: full opacity at act start, then fades — the hero form |
| `"0 1 0 0"` | **greet and hold**: full at p=0, no ramp either end |

**The plateau is the point.** Without one, a cue is a triangle that touches full
opacity for a single instant, so the reader has to stop on exactly the right
pixel to see the line at full strength and every heading reads slightly faded.
`"0.1 0.9 0.15 0.4"` — fast in, long slow out — is the confident form. Cue
windows on a pinned act **overlap by design**, roughly 15% of the act: the
outgoing line is still fading while the next arrives, and a gap between cues
reads as a loading failure.

Five rules, each one a real bug this fixture has caught:

- **A hero cue needs the greet form.** A plain `"0 0.7"` means the first
  screen every visitor sees has no headline on it.
- **The last act's cue must hold** (one value). A two-value close cue fades
  the CTA out before the page ends.
- **Only the last act may hold.** A one-value cue on a *middle* pinned act
  stays lit through the whole un-pin slide — the line travels a full viewport
  up, crosses fixed chrome, overlaps the next section. Invisible until
  measured; shows up as a contrast failure nobody meant.
- **Ground or greet.** A pinned stage is fully visible ~1vh *before* its own
  progress leaves 0. A plain two-value first cue shows an empty stage for
  that whole travel — give the act a ground (image/colour already doing
  work) or open with a greet cue.
- **Clip time ≠ cue time.** A `scrub` clip is mapped across the stage's
  *entire visible life* (default), not across the pinned travel, because the
  stage is on screen for a viewport before the pin starts and after it ends.
  Cues keep using `p` (they belong to the pin); the clip uses a separately
  computed `vp`. Reaching for `data-sc-clip-map="travel"` reintroduces the
  freeze — there's almost no reason to.

Two more that a harness will not catch by itself:

- **Pan overflow must be measured, not assumed.** The rail travels exactly
  `scrollWidth - viewport`; a rail narrower than the viewport travels **zero**
  and the act reads as a still. `rail.scrollWidth - innerWidth` — check it,
  don't guess.
- **Parallax rate is hundreds of pixels total, not a viewport fraction** — see
  the table above. A rate of 0.35 across three viewport-heights of scroll is
  35px: invisible.

Composing an act: devices stack (a pinned stage can hold a scrub clip, a
parallax layer, a kinetic headline, a spotlight at once), but one thing is the
reason the act exists — say that thing in one sentence or the act has none.

## The playhead is lerped (§1)

The mechanism the whole kit's smoothness rests on, and the one F-012 kept
being blamed on. **Scroll never writes `currentTime`.** It writes a *target*,
and a standalone rAF loop walks the clip toward that target at a fixed
fraction per frame:

> *"Wheel events do not arrive at a constant rate, so a 1:1 write reproduces
> every gap in them and the clip reads as a stutter rather than a glide."*

Three mechanisms, all on by default:

- **Lerp 0.18 per frame.** `data-sc-lerp` overrides it, on the mount root for
  the whole page or on a single `<video>`. **Clamped to 0.02–1 and never read
  as 0** — a 0 lerp is a playhead that never moves. Reach for an override only
  when a page's clips are short enough that 0.18 visibly lags the hand.
  Worldflight wants 0.12 instead; see [`pace.md`](pace.md).
- **Deadband: 8 ms desktop, 20 ms mobile.** A write smaller than that costs a
  seek and shows nothing; on a phone it costs more than it shows.
- **Seek coalescing.** No seek is queued while the decoder is still resolving
  the last one. *"A fast flick otherwise piles seeks up and freezes the clip."*

An offscreen clip that has already reached its target stops being touched at
all. (Upstream states the offscreen skip without a threshold value; the 0.002
figure belongs to `shoot.mjs`'s settle test, below, not to this skip.)

This applies to **every** scrub clip on the page, act or worldflight. It is
also why the shooter waits for the playhead to arrive before each frame:

> *"A frame captured mid-lerp is a frame the page never actually holds."*

`shoot.mjs` settles on `|current − target| < 0.002 && !seeking`. Any harness
the chain runs against a scrubbed page inherits that requirement — a
screenshot taken mid-lerp makes the run unrepeatable, not merely imprecise.

Upstream also drops the damping to 1.0 (no smoothing at all) under reduced
motion. **That branch does not port: F-011.** The lerp is unconditional here,
which is the correct behaviour anyway — it is a smoothing mechanism, not an
effect, and turning it off is what produces the stepping fault.

## Layered scenes: where the premium feel comes from (§6)

Ported from `devices.md` § 6, measured off a reference premium site and proven
on a live build. A flat page moves as one sheet; a layered page is a stack of
cut-out planes sliding past each other, and *"the eye reads that differential
motion as depth before it reads anything else."* It is the single biggest
difference between a page that feels built and one that feels assembled, and
it costs three transparent images and a multiplier each.

- **Plan the planes back to front.** Far ridge, mid ridge, the product, then a
  **foreground plane in front of the product**. The product sits between mid
  and front, so the foreground overtakes it as the reader scrolls. That
  overtaking is the move.
- **Small rate differences, not big ones.** The reference hero lags the far
  plane **31%** behind the page, the mid plane **17%**, the product **20%**,
  and foreground and copy travel at exactly **1×**. Adjacent planes differ by
  **10–30%**. Larger stops reading as distance and starts reading as things
  sliding around. **Copy always rides at 1×.**
- **Shape the foreground for the product.** A straight-edged foreground covers
  the product's CTA within a few hundred pixels of scroll. Cut it so it dips
  where the product is and rises at the edges, and the button stays in view
  two to three times as long.
- **Every plane is solid below its silhouette.** Cut-out art that fades to
  transparent at the bottom lets the plane behind show through as the planes
  separate. Fill each column solid from its first opaque pixel down.
- **Fade the section floor.** Planes travel past the section's bottom edge and
  are clipped there. A gradient to the page ground over the last 200–300 px,
  layered above every plane, hides the clip line at any scroll position.

Three traps, each of which cost a round of fixes:

- A global `img { max-width: 100% }` shrinks an absolutely positioned plane to
  the viewport on phones, so the far layer never shows. **Planes carry
  `max-width: none` and a fixed pixel width.**
- **Never `transition: transform` on a parallaxed element.** A reveal class is
  the usual culprit. The transition eases every per-frame scroll write over
  its own duration, and on a phone that reads as the product lagging a full
  second behind the thumb. Parallaxed elements transition **opacity only**.
- Replacing a plane's art under the same filename ships nothing to a phone
  holding the old bytes. **New art gets a new name.**

`data-sc-parallax` and a raw scroll multiplier are the same tool in different
units. What matters is the **ratio between planes**, not the absolute travel.

## The premium fade-in, exactly (§8)

The `flow` + `in` device is most of the page, so its defaults decide how the
page feels between the acts:

| Ingredient | Value |
|---|---|
| Opacity | 0 → 1 |
| Rise | **~14 px** |
| Duration | **~620 ms**, ease-out |
| Stagger | **30–80 ms**, children in reading order |
| Trigger | IntersectionObserver, `-12%` bottom root margin, **fires once** |

- **A fade with no rise reads as a loading glitch.** A rise **past 24 px reads
  as a slide.** 14 px is the band, not a starting point to tune upward.
- The `-12%` margin fires the reveal when the reader is looking, not when the
  first pixel clears the fold.
- `data-sc-in` is what the engine watches. Without it nothing fires and the
  stagger children stay hidden.
- **Content that re-hides on the way back up is a defect, not an effect.**
- *"Larger, slower, or bouncier is never more premium; the restraint is the
  signal."*

**A flow section directly after a pinned act takes reduced padding.** The
pinned stage needs a full viewport to scroll off, and full `--sc-section`
padding on top of that delays the flow section's first content by another
screen. The harness will not call it dead scroll — correctly, the stage is
moving — and the reader still sees a near-empty screen. Cut the block padding
there and start the first reveal near `p = 0`.

## Rail settle on `pan` (§3)

Lateral travel alone reads as a slideshow on rails. **Give the rail's items a
staggered settle driven from `--sc-p`** and they read as a drawer being
pulled instead.

- **Exempt the first item** — a `pan` act needs its opening content already
  present.
- **Floor the opacity around 0.55**, so a not-yet-settled card reads as
  arriving rather than as failing to load.

Upstream gates the settle to `prefers-reduced-motion` — **utgår, F-011**.
The settle always runs. What *does* survive from
the same passage is the reachability requirement, which is not a motion
preference at all: a `pan` rail's transform **is** the navigation, so nothing
may zero it and park the act on its first screenful. Every item in a rail
stays reachable, and that is checked on the sheet, not assumed.

Two more, from the same section:

- **Card copy is read while cropped.** Items enter and leave through the
  viewport edges, so a heading is half-shown for most of its life, and two
  half-headings side by side can read as a third word (`TRACE` beside
  `EVALUATE` becoming `RE EVALUATE`). Keep card headings to one or two short
  words and expect every line to be read partially cut off.
- If three items do not reach half a viewport of overflow, **the fix is more
  rail, not wider cards**: put the act's heading in as the first item and a
  closing note as the last. Both earn their place, and they add the width the
  travel needs.

## Devices that cannot share an element (§9)

**`magnet`, `parallax` and `cue` all write `transform`.** The magnet writes
every frame in its own rAF loop, so it silently wins and the cue's entrance
rise is discarded — a visible animation lost to a race, with nothing in the
console.

- On a magnetic CTA, set **`data-sc-rise="0"`** so the cue writes a no-op
  instead of losing to the magnet.
- A cued element that wants its own continuous transform drives an **inner
  wrapper** from `--sc-p` in CSS, rather than stacking a second device on the
  same node.

All three pointer devices **interpolate toward** the pointer rather than
tracking it directly: *"direct tracking reads as artificial because it carries
no momentum."* They stay gated to `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` so
touch never fires a false hover — that gate is a pointer-capability query, not
a motion preference, and it stands.
The reduced-motion half of the same sentence does not port (F-011).

## Kinetic type: the mask and the re-split (§5)

Each unit slides up from **behind a mask**, so it enters from a clean edge
rather than simply fading.

- **Line masks must reserve room for descenders.** A mask clipped to the line
  box shears the tails off g, y, p and j, *"and that is the single most common
  way this effect looks broken."*
- **Line splitting measures real line boxes, so it re-runs after
  `document.fonts.ready`.** Do not call it on text still loading its face. The
  same `fonts.ready` handle earns its place twice over: a webfont swapping in
  changes the measured height of every copy block, so anything sized against
  those blocks (a scrim plate, a rail) is wrong until it re-measures.
- Lines are almost always right; words for a short punch line; characters
  approximately never, *"because it turns reading into waiting."*
- **One kinetic headline per act, at most.**

## What makes a `count` land (§7)

- **Ease out, hard.** A cubic ease-out, so most of the distance goes by in the
  first third and the last digits settle slowly. *"A linear count reads as a
  slot machine."*
- **1.2–1.8 s.** Under a second and the reader misses that it moved; past two
  and they are waiting for a number they have already guessed.
- **Fires at half visibility, once**, so the reader is looking at it when it
  starts, and it never re-runs on the way back up.
- **Pair it with the fade.** A counter inside a `data-sc-in` stack rises in
  with its label and starts ticking as it arrives — *"the same numbers static
  on the page read as a spreadsheet."*
- Write the target exactly as it should render, commas included; the engine
  strips them before parsing and applies `tabular-nums` so the layout does not
  jitter.

**A concept, fictional or pre-launch brand has no verified figures, so it has
no counters.** The device suits a SaaS or agency page and will look good in
the score table, *"which is exactly the trap: every number you could put in it
would be invented."* Decide this before designing an act around a number, not
after. Real brand, real stats, or a different device.

## Appendix: pattern vocabulary

Named patterns from taste-skill § 10, carried here so orchestrator, builder
and reviewer name the same thing. It is a **vocabulary, not a menu** — several
entries below are banned as directions elsewhere in the chain (glassmorphism,
holographic foil, carousels, gooey menus) and appear here only so a critique
can say which trope it is refusing.

- **Hero** — Asymmetric Split · Editorial Manifesto · Video/Media Mask ·
  Kinetic-Type · Curtain-Reveal · Scroll-Pinned.
- **Nav** — Dock Magnification · Magnetic Button (`data-sc-magnet`) · Gooey
  Menu · Dynamic Island · Contextual Radial · Floating Speed Dial · Mega Menu
  Reveal.
- **Layout** — Bento Grid · Masonry · Chroma Grid · Split-Screen Scroll ·
  Sticky-Stack Sections.
- **Cards** — Parallax Tilt Card (`data-sc-tilt`) · Spotlight Border Card
  (`data-sc-spotlight`) · Glassmorphism Panel · Holographic Foil ·
  Tinder Swipe Stack · Morphing Modal.
- **Scroll** — Sticky Scroll Stack · Horizontal Scroll Hijack (= `pan`) ·
  Locomotive / Sequence Scroll (= `scrub`) · Zoom Parallax · Scroll Progress
  Path · Liquid Swipe Transition.
- **Galleries** — Dome Gallery · Coverflow Carousel · Drag-to-Pan Grid ·
  Accordion Image Slider · Hover Image Trail · Glitch Effect Image.
- **Type** — Kinetic Marquee · **Text Mask Reveal** (massive type as a
  transparent window onto video — this is K2's letter-window) · Text Scramble
  · Circular Text Path · Gradient Stroke Animation · Kinetic Typography Grid.
- **Micro** — Particle Explosion Button · Liquid Pull-to-Refresh · Skeleton
  Shimmer · Directional Hover-Aware Button · Ripple Click · Animated SVG Line
  Drawing · Mesh Gradient Background · Lens Blur Depth.

Names alone are not permission. A pattern still has to clear the fingerprint
gate, the register, and `../motion.md` before it ships.

engine: the console then says `[scrollcraft] act "…" will not pin: its stage computes
position:relative` and every pinned act scrolls away, leaving its spacer as dead scroll.

1	# Feeling curve, peak, signature move, fingerprint gate
2	
3	Condensed from `upstream/scroll-craft/.../references/feel.md` and
4	`uniqueness.md` §§3–4. Design the feeling before the acts: a device chosen
5	before the emotion is a device looking for a reason.
6	
7	## The feeling curve
8	
9	One line per act in `BRIEF.md`, written **before a single act exists**: the
10	emotion, then what on screen causes it. The emotion is the constraint; the
11	device name only ever appears in the cause column, second.
12	
13	```
14	1  Recognition   their own kitchen counter at 7am, shot at eye height
15	2  Fatigue       the two containers, the mess, held still while copy names it
16	3  Delight       a wipe, and the whole frame is one cold can, condensation running
17	4  Trust         macro texture at a scale the eye cannot get in a shop
18	5  Appetite      the flavours travelling sideways, each one landing whole
19	6  Resolve       everything stops, one can, one line, one place to buy it
20	```
21	
22	Two adjacent acts with the same feeling means one is filler — cut it or
23	change what it does. The curve outranks the Step 1 journey beats: beats say
24	what the visitor learns, the curve says what they feel while learning it, and
25	where they disagree the curve wins.
26	
27	## The peak
28	
29	People remember one peak and the ending; the middle compresses into a general
30	impression. So every build engineers **one** deliberate peak, named in
31	`BRIEF.md` as the sentence a visitor would say to a friend ("the screen went
32	black and then the whole ocean lit up under me" — a moment, not "the hero is
33	impressive"). The peak gets, at the expense of every other act:
34	
35	| It gets | Because |
36	|---|---|
37	| The asset budget | Best generated frames or the only real footage go here |
38	| The silence before it | A quiet act or empty viewport, so the change has something to be a change from |
39	| The most scroll room | Largest `data-sc-span` on the page, `dwell` tuned to settle exactly there |
40	
41	A page with three peaks has none — demote the losers (shorter span, plainer
42	device). The close must resolve, not trail off: the divider collapses, the
43	world lands somewhere, the type quiets — never a fade to an empty stage.
44	
45	## The tell-someone test
46	
47	Complete, before building: *"it's the site where ___."* "It has a scrub
48	video" is a device name — no hook. "You drag the letters of the logo apart
49	and they snap back perfectly" is an experience — that's a hook. The blank has
50	to be something that happened **to the visitor**. This sentence usually
51	contains the signature move; if the tell-someone sentence and the signature
52	move point at different moments, one of them is decoration.
53	
54	## The signature move
55	
56	One bespoke interaction that exists on this build alone — coded in the page
57	off `--sc-p` or a page-authored `data-sc-*`, never a parameter on a kit
58	device, never in any prior build. The engine stays untouched.
59	
60	**What counts** (upstream examples, not a menu to pick from): scroll-as-
61	playhead over a persistent trace rail; a wordmark the pointer pulls apart and
62	snaps back exactly; a line drawing whose `stroke-dashoffset` is driven from
63	`--sc-p`; a running receipt that accumulates real figures; one control that
64	regrades the whole page at once (time-of-day, temperature, load).
65	
66	**What does not count**: a recoloured/resized spotlight; `data-sc-tilt` turned
67	up; a different easing on kinetic lines; more cards in a rail; a third
68	`scrub` act; anything the engine already does under a project class name.
69	Test: describe the move to someone who has seen the other builds — if they
70	can't tell it apart from something the kit already does, it isn't one.
71	
72	## Being in it, not watching it
73	
74	Upstream `feel.md` § 4. *"A film plays whether you are there or not. The
75	difference between a viewer and a participant is whether the page acknowledges
76	that somebody specific is here: how fast they are moving, where their pointer
77	is, whether they stopped."*
78	
79	Five techniques, in the kit's own vocabulary:
80	
81	- **Pointer parallax that moves the world, not a card.** `data-sc-spotlight`
82	  publishes `--sc-mx` / `--sc-my`. Drive a *background layer's* transform off
83	  them instead of a highlight, and the environment shifts as the visitor
84	  moves, slightly, the way a real space does when you lean.
85	- **Dwell-triggered detail.** Hold still on an act and something further
86	  arrives — a caption, a second line, a small annotation. Reward for stopping.
87	  Mechanically: **read `--sc-p` staying constant across a few frames**, in the
88	  page's own JS, and reveal something that was **never needed for
89	  comprehension**.
90	- **Scroll velocity shaping intensity.** Fast scrolling raises grain, blur,
91	  chromatic offset, ground saturation; slow scrolling settles it. *"The page
92	  feels like it is being driven rather than played back, and it costs one
93	  derived custom property."*
94	- **The page addressing "you" at one moment that lands.** Not throughout,
95	  which is just copywriting. **One line**, at the emotional turn, in second
96	  person, when the visitor is already implicated. *"It works because it is the
97	  only time."*
98	- **A trace of where they have been.** Anything that accumulates as they
99	  travel, so arriving at the end means having a record rather than reaching a
100	  footer.
101	
102	**Embodiment is seasoning. One or two per page.** *"A page that reacts to
103	everything feels haunted, not alive: the visitor stops reading and starts
104	poking, which is the opposite of what any of this is for."* Pick the one that
105	serves the peak and leave the rest.

# Feeling curve, peak, signature move, fingerprint gate

Condensed from `upstream/scroll-craft/.../references/feel.md` and
`uniqueness.md` §§3–4. Design the feeling before the acts: a device chosen
before the emotion is a device looking for a reason.

## The feeling curve

One line per act in `BRIEF.md`, written **before a single act exists**: the
emotion, then what on screen causes it. The emotion is the constraint; the
device name only ever appears in the cause column, second.

```
1  Recognition   their own kitchen counter at 7am, shot at eye height
2  Fatigue       the two containers, the mess, held still while copy names it
3  Delight       a wipe, and the whole frame is one cold can, condensation running
4  Trust         macro texture at a scale the eye cannot get in a shop
5  Appetite      the flavours travelling sideways, each one landing whole
6  Resolve       everything stops, one can, one line, one place to buy it
```

Two adjacent acts with the same feeling means one is filler — cut it or
change what it does. The curve outranks the Step 1 journey beats: beats say
what the visitor learns, the curve says what they feel while learning it, and
where they disagree the curve wins.

## The peak

People remember one peak and the ending; the middle compresses into a general
impression. So every build engineers **one** deliberate peak, named in
`BRIEF.md` as the sentence a visitor would say to a friend ("the screen went
black and then the whole ocean lit up under me" — a moment, not "the hero is
impressive"). The peak gets, at the expense of every other act:

| It gets | Because |
|---|---|
| The asset budget | Best generated frames or the only real footage go here |
| The silence before it | A quiet act or empty viewport, so the change has something to be a change from |
| The most scroll room | Largest `data-sc-span` on the page, `dwell` tuned to settle exactly there |

A page with three peaks has none — demote the losers (shorter span, plainer
device). The close must resolve, not trail off: the divider collapses, the
world lands somewhere, the type quiets — never a fade to an empty stage.

## The tell-someone test

Complete, before building: *"it's the site where ___."* "It has a scrub
video" is a device name — no hook. "You drag the letters of the logo apart
and they snap back perfectly" is an experience — that's a hook. The blank has
to be something that happened **to the visitor**. This sentence usually
contains the signature move; if the tell-someone sentence and the signature
move point at different moments, one of them is decoration.

## The signature move

One bespoke interaction that exists on this build alone — coded in the page
off `--sc-p` or a page-authored `data-sc-*`, never a parameter on a kit
device, never in any prior build. The engine stays untouched.

**What counts** (upstream examples, not a menu to pick from): scroll-as-
playhead over a persistent trace rail; a wordmark the pointer pulls apart and
snaps back exactly; a line drawing whose `stroke-dashoffset` is driven from
`--sc-p`; a running receipt that accumulates real figures; one control that
regrades the whole page at once (time-of-day, temperature, load).

**What does not count**: a recoloured/resized spotlight; `data-sc-tilt` turned
up; a different easing on kinetic lines; more cards in a rail; a third
`scrub` act; anything the engine already does under a project class name.
Test: describe the move to someone who has seen the other builds — if they
can't tell it apart from something the kit already does, it isn't one.

## Being in it, not watching it

Upstream `feel.md` § 4. *"A film plays whether you are there or not. The
difference between a viewer and a participant is whether the page acknowledges
that somebody specific is here: how fast they are moving, where their pointer
is, whether they stopped."*

Five techniques, in the kit's own vocabulary:

- **Pointer parallax that moves the world, not a card.** `data-sc-spotlight`
  publishes `--sc-mx` / `--sc-my`. Drive a *background layer's* transform off
  them instead of a highlight, and the environment shifts as the visitor
  moves, slightly, the way a real space does when you lean.
- **Dwell-triggered detail.** Hold still on an act and something further
  arrives — a caption, a second line, a small annotation. Reward for stopping.
  Mechanically: **read `--sc-p` staying constant across a few frames**, in the
  page's own JS, and reveal something that was **never needed for
  comprehension**.
- **Scroll velocity shaping intensity.** Fast scrolling raises grain, blur,
  chromatic offset, ground saturation; slow scrolling settles it. *"The page
  feels like it is being driven rather than played back, and it costs one
  derived custom property."*
- **The page addressing "you" at one moment that lands.** Not throughout,
  which is just copywriting. **One line**, at the emotional turn, in second
  person, when the visitor is already implicated. *"It works because it is the
  only time."*
- **A trace of where they have been.** Anything that accumulates as they
  travel, so arriving at the end means having a record rather than reaching a
  footer.

**Embodiment is seasoning. One or two per page.** *"A page that reacts to
everything feels haunted, not alive: the visitor stops reading and starts
poking, which is the opposite of what any of this is for."* Pick the one that
serves the peak and leave the rest.

These are gated to `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — a pointer-capability
query, which stands.
Upstream also turns them off under reduced motion — **that half utgår, F-011**.
The rule that does survive is upstream's own:
*"a technique that only exists on desktop cannot be the thing that carries the
page's meaning."*

## Pacing as emotion

Upstream `feel.md` § 5. *"Scroll distance is emotional time. It is the only
clock this medium has, and it is fully under your control, which makes it the
cheapest emotional instrument in the kit and the one most often left at
default."*

| Pacing | Reads as | Built with |
|---|---|---|

| A long pin | Held breath, pressure, attention | `data-sc-span` 3+, overlapping cues, one idea |
| An empty viewport before a reveal | Silence before the drop | A ground-only act, no cue until the next one |
| A slow settle mid-act | The shot landing | `data-sc-dwell` 0.35–0.6, cue peak on the settle |
| A fast cue with a long plateau | Confidence, arrival | `data-sc-cue="0.1 0.9 0.08 0.4"` |
| A slow ramp in | Hesitation, dawning | Long `rampIn` — **once per page**, it is close to feeling broken |

Four rules follow:

- **Silence must be authored, not left over.** *"An empty screen you meant
  reads as anticipation. An empty screen you did not mean reads as a page that
  failed to load, and the harness reports both as dead scroll."* If the empty
  viewport before the peak is deliberate, **say so in `BRIEF.md`** so the
  verification pass can tell it from dead scroll. This is the sentence that
  keeps `scroll_verify.py`'s `blankBands` check from being either useless or a
  false alarm.
- **Give the peak room.** The peak act has the largest span on the page by a
  visible margin. *"If every act is 2.2 vh, the page has no shape, whatever
  the curve in BRIEF.md says."*
- **Compress the administrative parts.** Specs, logistics, FAQ, credentials
  are information, not experience — flow sections at short stagger, never
  pinned acts with dwell. Spending scroll on them spends the visitor's
  patience on the part they will not remember.
- **A continuous world is the exception to pacing variety.** All of the above
  is about a page of *acts*. A worldflight is one camera move, and *"a camera
  that changes speed between legs reads as broken rather than as

  the single long leg — [`pace.md`](pace.md).

The total-length budget stays **8–14 viewport-heights**. Pacing is how that
budget is spent, not permission to spend more: *"a page that needs 20 vh to
land its curve has too many acts, not too little room."*

## The fingerprint gate

Registry: `VAULT/wiki/projects/_index/design-fingerprints.md`, per-vault,
starting from whatever rows already exist — not repeating **yourself** across
builds, not a universal constraint. **Six dimensions**, recorded per row:

| # | Dimension | What it records |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Grammar | Which of `grammars.md`, or a named new one |
| 2 | Nav treatment | What the chrome is and what it's for |
| 3 | Hero device | What the first screen does |
| 4 | Act-sequence shape | Device order, act count, total viewport-heights |
| 5 | Close pattern | How the last screen behaves, what the CTA sits in |
| 6 | Signature move | The one bespoke interaction, in a phrase |

**The gate: a new build must differ from EVERY existing row on at least 4 of
the 6** — four against each row individually, not averaged across the table.
Dimension 6 is free (unique by definition), so the gate really asks for 3
more out of the remaining 5 against each row. If the plan fails, **change
the plan, not the log** — rewriting a row to fit is what makes it worthless.

**Row format** — one row per shipped build, all six dimensions plus a world
note and the path: `| Build | Grammar | Nav | Hero device | Act-sequence
shape | Close pattern | Signature move | Register | World / palette | Path |`

**Rows are append-only.** From upstream `templates/FINGERPRINTS.md`:

> *"A build that has been superseded stays in the table, because the space it
> occupies is still occupied."*

A replaced, retired or rejected build keeps its row. The registry does not
record what is live; it records what surface has already been taken, and a
surface stays taken whether or not the build that claimed it is still up.
Deleting a row silently frees a shape for reuse, which is the same failure as

31	the same footage reads as one continuous move. Same clips, same damping, same engine —
32	only the weights changed.

35	one movement.**

38	
39	The instinct is to spend as little scroll as possible. A fly-through wants the
40	opposite: the reader is steering a camera, and a camera that answers too eagerly feels
41	twitchy.
42	
43	| | Value |
44	|---|---|
45	| Floor for a world you fly through | **0.21–0.22 vh per second of film** |
46	| What the per-8s line yields | 0.14–0.19 vh/s — *noticeably fast* |
47	| What the per-8s line actually is | a **dead-scroll guardrail, not a taste ceiling** |
48	
49	Exceeding the guardrail is fine and often correct; exceeding it *without checking* is
50	not. The harness defines dead scroll mechanically and will tell you. At 0.216 vh/s a
51	0.12 vh sample gap still advances the clip by half a second — nowhere near dead.

54

56	> surging."*
57	
58	| Knob | Act page | Worldflight | Why the flight differs |
59	|---|---|---|---|
60	| `data-sc-lerp` | 0.18 (default) | **0.12** | A flight has more legs mounted and more seams than an act page, and the extra damping is what actually removes wheel-event judder |

1	# The lift — what replaces "just run polish"
2	
3	`impeccable polish` is a *last* pass and says so: it "preserves the incumbent visual
4	world" and "does not add animation merely to make polish visible". Pointed at a whole
5	page that is merely competent, it returns a slightly tidier competent page. Every other
6	impeccable command ends by handing off to polish; polish is the handoff target, not the
7	procedure.
8	
9	The lift is the procedure. Each pass is a named skill invocation, in an order the
10	upstream references themselves prescribe, with a mechanical gate between passes.
11	
12	## The sequence
13	
14	| # | Pass | Invocation | Output |
15	|---|---|---|---|
16	| 1 | Read-only review | [`verbs/review.md`](verbs/review.md) — slop audit + `Skill(a11y-audit)` + [`verbs/critique.md`](verbs/critique.md) + `Skill(review-animations)` | One ranked table, ≤ 15 rows, Block or Approve |
17	| 2 | The quartet, in parallel | `design-critic`, `design-heuristics`, `design-a11y-reviewer`, `design-perf-reviewer` | Four reports on the shared contract below |
18	| 3 | Where motion belongs | `Skill(find-animation-opportunities)` + `Skill(animation-vocabulary)` | ≤ 5 proposals with exact values **and a Rejected list** |
19	| 4 | Fix plans | `improve-animations`' PLAN-TEMPLATE per finding | `plans/NNN-slug.md`: Problem / Target / Conventions / Steps / Boundaries / Verification incl. a feel-check |
20	| 5 | Fix passes, one per round | (a) `impeccable layout` → (b) `impeccable typeset` → (c) `impeccable colorize` *only if* the critique says flat or grey → (d) `Skill(animate)` + `Skill(emil-design-eng)` → (e) `impeccable delight` *only if* the brief carries a delight thesis → (f) the copy gate → (g) `impeccable harden` → (h) `impeccable optimize` against the probe reports → (i) `impeccable polish` **last** | One commit per pass, screenshots after each |
21	| 6 | Mechanical gate after every pass | `detect.mjs --json`, `preflight_taste.py`, `scroll_verify.py`, `perf_probe.py`, `motion_probe.py`, `contrast_over_media.py` | All green before the next pass |
22	| 7 | Round again | Back to 1 | Stop when a whole pass finds nothing material **and the critic writes "beats" for each locked reference** |
23	
24	Cap: six rounds per cell. Then stop and hand Anton a table of what is still open, rather
25	than iterating quietly forever.
26	
27	## Triage order inside a round
28	
29	From `impeccable/reference/polish.md`: **broken → states → flow and hierarchy → visual →
30	code.** A colour decision taken before a broken state is fixed is a decision taken about
31	the wrong page. Within "visual", most material first: a fix that changes what the page
32	*is* outranks one that changes how it is finished.
33	
34	## The reviewer contract
35	
36	All four reviewers return the same shape, borrowed from impeccable's finish-reviewer:
37	
38	1. First line, one disposition word: `recapture` · `rebuild` · `fix` · `ship`.
39	2. Then exactly five sections:
40	   - **persistence** — did the previous round's fixes survive?
41	   - **fidelity** — against the target picture, screen by screen (F-007).
42	   - **ceiling** — what each locked reference still does better, one line per reference.
43	   - **material_fixes** — at most 8, most material first, each with a target value or a
44	     reference image, never "make it nicer".
45	   - **keep** — what must not be touched.
46	
47	The critic's ceiling section carries the honest sentence **per locked reference**:
48	"beats garden-eight on X, loses to mattis-studio on Y". A single lump verdict hides which
49	reference is actually beating you.
50	
51	Reconciliation when they disagree: **accessibility > performance > usability > brief >
52	personas > escalate**. Performance sits above usability because a page that drops frames
53	cannot be judged on usability at all.
54	
55	Every finding is verified against the pixels by whoever merges the reports. A reviewer
56	report is a claim, not a fact.
57	
58	## When a pass is skipped
59	
60	`bolder`, `quieter` and `distill` run **only** when pass 1 or 2 says a named section is
61	flat, loud or overloaded. `colorize` runs only on a flatness finding. `delight` runs only
62	when the brief declares a delight thesis. Skipping is the default; running one without a
63	finding behind it is how a page drifts away from its own direction.
64	
65	## Not part of the lift
66	
67	- `impeccable live` — needs a dev server and an overlay; it is Anton's own manual
68	  iteration after delivery, not a chain step.
69	- `impeccable onboard` / `extract` — Operate surfaces and design-system maintenance.
70	- `impeccable document` — runs *after* ship, from the built code, never before.
71	- `prototype` — the bake-off already has `board.py`.
72	- The gstack quartet (`design-review`, `design-shotgun`, `design-html`,
73	  `design-consultation`) — a parallel pipeline. Pick one lane per project; what is worth
74	  borrowing from it is already ported into `verbs/review.md`.
75	
76	## Stopping
77	
78	Two conditions, both required: a full pass 1–2 that finds nothing material, and the
79	critic writing "beats" for every locked reference. "Stands up beside them" is not the
80	bar. If you cannot say it yet, the page is not finished — and if you have said it six
81	times without it becoming true, the concept is what needs changing, not the polish.

# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

Källa: `tests/alunix-ab-r7/PROMPT.md`, avsnitten "Alunix, fakta", "Copy som ska användas
ordagrant" och "Förbjudet, bindande". Ingen annan källa har använts. Står det inte där står
det inte här.

## Platform

web

Belägg: de tre exempelsajterna är `.html`-filer under `/sites/` som serveras live och visas i
`<iframe>` från samma origin.

## Users

Vi vänder oss till verksamheter som behöver en webbplats. Sidan tilltalar dem i andra person,
"er" och "ni", aldrig "jag". De verksamhetstyper vi faktiskt kan visa upp är florist,
restaurang och konferens, eftersom det är vad de tre exempelsajterna är.

Vad de behöver av oss står i rubriken och ingen annanstans: `Er hemsida är nutidens
visitkort`. Vi vet alltså vad sidan lovar dem. Vi vet inte hur de köper, när de köper eller
vad de jämför med. Ingen intervju finns.

Ingen ytterligare målgrupp är bekräftad. Bransch, storlek och köpsituation är öppna frågor,
inte fakta.

## Product Purpose

Alunix är en webbyrå i Sverige. Sidan säljer en tjänst: webbdesign.

Vi skapar skräddarsydda webbplatser. Underraden är låst och lyder ordagrant: `Vi skapar
skräddarsydda webbplatser som hjälper er att exponera verksamheten.`

Erbjudandet är samlat: `Webbdesign, design och system. Allt på ett ställe.` Tjänsterna är tre
och numrerade 01 till 03: `Design`, `Utveckling`, `System`. Var och en får en kort underrad i
byråröst, utan påståenden om kunder eller resultat.

Tesrubriken är `VI BYGGER ERT VARUMÄRKE.`

Prisrubriken är `Alla har rätt till bra design.`

## Positioning

Vi visar vad vi kan i stället för att påstå det. Byrån visar sitt arbete genom tre riktiga
exempelsajter som ligger i samma repo och serveras live. De får visas live i `<iframe>`, samma
origin när sidan serveras från repo-roten, och de ska vara användbara när de är öppna. En
besökare kan alltså använda arbetet direkt på sidan, inte bara titta på en bild av det.

Tre saker till skiljer erbjudandet: design, utveckling och system kommer från samma ställe;
två av tre paket har ett pris utskrivet på sidan; och prislöftet är formulerat som en
principsats, `Alla har rätt till bra design.`

## Operating Context

- De tre exempelsajterna ligger i samma repo som sidan och serveras live därifrån.
- Ramarna är samma origin när sidan serveras från repo-roten.
- En ram som visats får aldrig transformeras eller tonas efteråt. Den ska gå att använda.
- Skärmbilder av de tre sajterna ligger i `assets/demo-calyx.webp`, `assets/demo-horai.webp`
  och `assets/demo-hyperborea.webp`.
- Logotypen ligger i `assets/logo-white.svg` och `assets/logo-black.svg` och får läggas inline.
- Allt material ligger i `assets/`. Inga egna Unsplash-anrop och ingen egen server.
- Servern är `python ~/.agents/skills/design/scripts/serve.py --port <port>` från repo-roten.
- Kontakt sker via e-post. Det finns inget formulär som skickar någonstans.

## Capabilities and Constraints

**Tre paket.** Raderna och priserna är låsta och skrivs ordagrant:

| Paket | Pris |
|---|---|
| `Standardpaket. Webbplats med CMS för egna ändringar och en första SEO-optimering.` | `26 900 kr` |
| `Paket med bokningssystem, betalning och kunddatabas.` | `38 900 kr` |
| `Helt skräddarsydda lösningar för produktkataloger, specialbyggda system med mera` | `Pris vid förfrågan` |

**Tre tjänster.** `Design`, `Utveckling`, `System`, numrerade 01 till 03, en kort underrad var.

**En kontaktväg.** `kontakt@alunix.se`, både som text och som mailto. Inget formulär.

**Tre exempelsajter, live.** Se Evidence on Hand.

**Bindande begränsningar i allt vi bygger:**

- Inga påhittade tal, kunder, omdömen, citat, logotypväggar, stjärnor eller "nöjda kunder".
- Inga tankstreck i synlig text.
- Inget "jag".
- Inga foton som läses som "vårt kontor" eller "vårt team".
- Inga hexfärger och inga typsnitt hämtade ur någon annan färdig mall.

**Öppet, inte bestämt:** vad de tre tjänsternas underrader säger ordagrant. De ska vara korta
och i byråröst, men texten är inte skriven.

## Brand Commitments

**Namn.** Alunix. Ett förbjudet namn finns, se Absences.

**Röst.** Byråröst i vi-form. Korta satser. Fakta före adjektiv. Svenska. Inget "jag". Inga
tankstreck i synlig text.

**Låst copy, copy-gate.** Följande rader bevaras ordagrant och skrivs aldrig om:

- `Er hemsida är nutidens visitkort`
- `Vi skapar skräddarsydda webbplatser som hjälper er att exponera verksamheten.`
- `VI BYGGER ERT VARUMÄRKE.`
- `Webbdesign, design och system. Allt på ett ställe.`
- `Design`, `Utveckling`, `System`
- `Standardpaket. Webbplats med CMS för egna ändringar och en första SEO-optimering.`
- `26 900 kr`
- `Paket med bokningssystem, betalning och kunddatabas.`
- `38 900 kr`
- `Helt skräddarsydda lösningar för produktkataloger, specialbyggda system med mera`
- `Pris vid förfrågan`
- `Alla har rätt till bra design.`
- `kontakt@alunix.se`
- `Exempelsida: Calyx, florist i Stockholm`
- `Exempelsida: Hōrai, Asian fusion-koncept`
- `Exempelsida: Hyperborea, konferens i Lund`

**Logotyp.** `assets/logo-white.svg` och `assets/logo-black.svg`. Får läggas inline.

**Dagens register, som jämförelse och inte som lås.** Kall nästan svart `#17181B`. Blå
`#1E5E9C` bara för handling. Geist för rubrik, Inter för brödtext, JetBrains Mono för data.
Ett nytt koncept får avvika helt från det.

## Evidence on Hand

Detta är hela beviskassan. Inget annat får synas på sidan.

**Tre exempelsajter, live i `<iframe>`, med sina låsta bildtexter:**

| Sajt | Fil | Rad att använda |
|---|---|---|
| Calyx | `/sites/calyx.html` | `Exempelsida: Calyx, florist i Stockholm` |
| Hōrai | `/sites/horai.html` | `Exempelsida: Hōrai, Asian fusion-koncept` |
| Hyperborea | `/sites/hyperborea.html` | `Exempelsida: Hyperborea, konferens i Lund` |

De tre exempelsajterna är de enda kunder som får synas.

**Skärmbilder av dem:** `assets/demo-calyx.webp`, `assets/demo-horai.webp`,
`assets/demo-hyperborea.webp`.

**Tre paket med pris:** `26 900 kr`, `38 900 kr`, `Pris vid förfrågan`, med paketraderna
ordagrant som de står under Capabilities and Constraints.

**En adress:** `kontakt@alunix.se`, som text och som mailto.

**Logotypfiler:** `assets/logo-white.svg`, `assets/logo-black.svg`.

**Ordagrann copy:** hela listan under Brand Commitments.

## Absences Future Work Must Not Fabricate

Inget av det här finns i beviskassan. Det får därför aldrig uppstå i en design, en bildtext,
en platshållare eller en bildprompt:

- Kunder utöver de tre exempelsajterna.
- Omdömen, recensioner och "nöjda kunder".
- Citat från någon utanför sidan.
- Logotypväggar.
- Stjärnor och betyg.
- Ett team att visa upp. Personer, porträtt, namn, roller.
- Ett kontor att visa upp. Inga foton som läses som "vårt kontor" eller "vårt team".
- Antal år i branschen.
- Antal projekt, antal kunder, antal leveranser.
- Påhittade tal överhuvudtaget. De enda siffrorna vi har är `26 900 kr` och `38 900 kr`, och
  tjänsternas numrering 01 till 03.
- Namnet Klova. Det får aldrig förekomma.

## Product Principles

1. **Beviset ska gå att använda, inte bara ses.** De tre sajterna är riktiga och körs live på
   sidan. Ramar som visats förblir användbara.
2. **Varje siffra på sidan är en siffra vi kan stå för.** Vi har två priser och en numrering.
   Fler tal finns inte, så fler tal skrivs inte.
3. **Priset står framme.** Två paket har ett utskrivet pris. Det tredje säger `Pris vid
   förfrågan` och inget annat.
4. **En adress, inget formulär.** `kontakt@alunix.se` är hela kontaktvägen, som text och som
   mailto.
5. **Vi talar i vi-form och kort.** Fakta före adjektiv. Aldrig "jag".

36	## Reading this table before a new build
37	
38	Three grammar collisions already exist among these seven rows: Calyx,
39	Hyperborea and Vintergatan all read as chaptered editorial, and Vinterspelen
40	leans the same way with a gallery inflection. A new chaptered-editorial build
41	has to clear 3 more dimensions against **each** of those four rows
42	individually — nav treatment and hero device are the two that repeat across
43	them most (folio/edition-strip nav, type-in-photo or split-poster heroes), so
44	those are the columns most likely to collide again. Hōrai and Tidvatten share
45	grammar (filmic one-shot), a fixed minimal bar, a JS-parallax full-bleed
46	hero, and a bell-curve-scrub pinned set-piece as their signature move's
47	underlying mechanism — a third filmic one-shot build with a scrub-driven
48	pinned set-piece would need a genuinely different mechanism for the move, not
49	just different numbers on screen, to clear dimension 6 meaningfully even
50	though the gate counts it as free.
51	
52	`before-ai-slop.html` is not a build to avoid colliding with — it is the
53	negative reference. Any real build should differ from it on every dimension
54	by construction.

111	R4, r4 M2) on top of the four seed rows, filmic one-shot has four (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
112	B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1) on top of two seed rows, and typographic poster has five (r1 K3, r2
113	R6, r6 A-K2 and B-K2, r7 B-K2). Continuous world is a five-row family (M1, V1, V2, V3,
114	V3b) that also shares nav treatment and close pattern by construction, because every r5
115	variant inherited M1's chrome and its two closing objects; those five rows clear the gate
116	against each other only on hero device, act shape and signature move, which is exactly 3
117	of the 5 non-free dimensions, the bare minimum. A sixth build in that family would have
118	nowhere left to differ.
119

121	scrolling top row with wordmark and contact (M1, V1, V2, V3, V3b) and the fixed minimal
122	bar with logo left and contact right that darkens or lightens per ground (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
123	B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1). Two hero devices likewise: the full-bleed blue-hour photograph
124	with a light-serif headline in the water (four rows) and the crushed poster wordmark with
125	the example screenshots showing through or beside the letters (four rows). The r7 rows
126	record their own shared dimensions honestly — each clears the gate at exactly 4 of 6
127	against its r6 predecessor, with grammar and nav knowingly shared — so a v3 of either
128	concept cannot reuse the hero device, the act shape or the close as well.
129	
130	Ten rows carried `?` in Register when the r1–r7 block was first appended: r2 R3, R4 and
131	R5, the r3 build, r4 M1 and M2, and r5 V1, V2, V3 and V3b. Those cells' own files name
132	grammar, world and palette but never a register from the six-name vocabulary, and no
133	sibling file names it for them either. On 2026-09-09 the column was filled for all ten by
134	reading each cell's `index.html` directly (and, for the r3 build and r4 M2, its 1440 fold
135	as pixels) against `design/SKILL.md`'s register table and its "what varies with register"
136	markers: face, grain, buttons versus typeset links, ground and subject. Every one of the
137	ten reads as **modern clean** — one lineage, sans display with mono as register only, no
138	serif and no grain anywhere, one blue accent, ledgers over cards, and a precision subject
139	— which is the same read the registry already recorded for r1 K1, K2, K5, K6 and r2 R1
140	and R2. Each cell states the file it was derived from, so the derivation is auditable and
141	declared as post-hoc, exactly like the seven seed rows above.

# Design fingerprint registry

The fingerprint gate for scroll-choreographed Persuade/Experience builds. See
`.agents/skills/design/references/scroll/feel-and-fingerprint.md` § The
fingerprint gate for the rule: **a new build must differ from EVERY existing
row on at least 4 of the 6 dimension columns**, checked row by row, not
averaged across the table. If a planned build fails the gate, change the
plan, not this file — rewriting a row to make a new build fit is the one
thing that makes this registry worthless.

Seeded 2026-09-03 with one row per existing example site in
`anti-slop-design/sites/`. These sites predate scroll-craft integration and
were not built against the nine-device kit or the eight named grammars — the
Grammar, Signature move and Register columns below are an honest read of what
each page actually does, mapped onto scroll-craft's vocabulary after the
fact, not a claim that they were built to it. Where a site has no bespoke
interaction beyond an ordinary reveal-on-scroll, the Signature move column
says `none` — that is a finding, not a gap in the audit.

No photography | ~7 sections: nav > hero > logo bar (6 fake wordmarks) > 3-icon feature-card grid > 4-stat metric grid > centred CTA > one-line footer | Plain centred CTA (heading/subhead/single pill button) trailing into a generic one-line copyright footer — trails off, no address or distinct voice | none — no bespoke interaction at all, not even a scroll reveal; static Tailwind hover states only | none of the six — generic gradient-on-white SaaS look, the anti-register the others are defined against | Inter; bg #FBFAF7, text #1F2937, gradient #6366F1→#8B5CF6→#EC4899, slate grays | `anti-slop-design/sites/before-ai-slop.html` |

## Reading this table before a new build

Three grammar collisions already exist among these seven rows: Calyx,
Hyperborea and Vintergatan all read as chaptered editorial, and Vinterspelen
leans the same way with a gallery inflection. A new chaptered-editorial build
has to clear 3 more dimensions against **each** of those four rows
individually — nav treatment and hero device are the two that repeat across
them most (folio/edition-strip nav, type-in-photo or split-poster heroes), so
those are the columns most likely to collide again. Hōrai and Tidvatten share
grammar (filmic one-shot), a fixed minimal bar, a JS-parallax full-bleed
hero, and a bell-curve-scrub pinned set-piece as their signature move's
underlying mechanism — a third filmic one-shot build with a scrub-driven
pinned set-piece would need a genuinely different mechanism for the move, not
just different numbers on screen, to clear dimension 6 meaningfully even
though the gate counts it as free.

`before-ai-slop.html` is not a build to avoid colliding with — it is the
negative reference. Any real build should differ from it on every dimension
by construction.

## Alunix concept builds, rounds 1–7 (appended 2026-09-09)

Twenty-nine rows, one per built `index.html` under `anti-slop-design/tests/alunix-*`.
Every column is derived from the cell's own files: the built HTML (nav markup, section
list, `data-sc-act` attributes, `:root` custom properties, font links), its `NOTES.md`
or `BRIEF.md`, and its desktop fold screenshot read as an image. Where a cell's own
files carry no evidence for a column, the cell says `?` rather than a guess — that is a
finding about the cell's documentation, not a licence to treat the dimension as free.

Duplicates were excluded, not counted twice: `alunix-ab-r6/board/cells/*` are byte-identical
copies of the seven r6 runs, `alunix-ab-r7/board/cells/K1-1` and `K2-1` are byte-identical
copies of r6 B-K1 and B-K2 placed on r7's comparison board, and
`alunix-concepts-r5/reference/V3-baseline` is a byte-identical copy of `V3-chain`.

Rounds 1–2 and 6 predate scroll-craft integration in those cells (no `data-sc-*` in the
markup); their act shapes are hand-rolled. Rounds 3–5 and 7 run the engine. In r6 and r7,
arm A is the Claude-native control (Anthropic's `frontend-design` system prompt, no skills,
no hooks) and arm B is this chain; `B-K1-nogate` is the r6 chain run where the gate never
fired, kept as its own row because it is a separate build.

### What these rows share, and what the next Alunix build has to avoid

Grammar has been spent hard. Chaptered editorial now has five rows here (r1 K4, r2 R2, R3,
R4, r4 M2) on top of the four seed rows, filmic one-shot has four (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1) on top of two seed rows, and typographic poster has five (r1 K3, r2
R6, r6 A-K2 and B-K2, r7 B-K2). Continuous world is a five-row family (M1, V1, V2, V3,
V3b) that also shares nav treatment and close pattern by construction, because every r5
variant inherited M1's chrome and its two closing objects; those five rows clear the gate
against each other only on hero device, act shape and signature move, which is exactly 3
of the 5 non-free dimensions, the bare minimum. A sixth build in that family would have

220	| r8 V3c Plåt i grunden, kortet vänds | Continuous world, loose reading inherited from M1 via V3b | Thin top row with wordmark and contact that scrolls away, inherited chrome | The same framed plate, now a two-faced card in a pinned act: headline outside it at poster scale, subline under it, and the plate itself turning on its Y axis from photographic front to matte black back | 7 screens, 1 pinned act (span 2.2, dwell 0.35) plus 6 flow acts; panel-open and panel-services removed, their content moved onto the card's back and into the ledger; two columns that swap material against each other | The price ledger and a mailto set as a line of type, no form, no repeated CTA | The hero plate is a physical card: `--flip = smoothstep(0.12, 0.72, --sc-ps)` turns `.plate-card` on rotateY so the light-pool front becomes a matte black back carrying the wordmark, hairline only at 90 degrees | Cinematic dark | Geist + Public Sans; `--sc-canvas` #0b0c0e, paper #fdfbf4, accent #1e5e9c | `anti-slop-design/tests/alunix-r8/runs/V3c/index.html` |
221	```
222	
223	**Varför detta fortfarande är en iteration och inte ett nytt bygge.** Grammatik, nav,
224	värld, palett och typsnitt är oförändrade från V3b, och de tre dimensioner som ändras
225	(hero-device, aktform, signatur) ändras alla av **samma** ingrepp: plåten blir ett kort med
226	två sidor. Ett nytt bygge skulle ha ändrat minst en av grammatik, nav eller värld; V3c
227	ändrar ingen av dem. Registrets V3-linje är därmed fortfarande upptagen av samma yta, nu
228	med en mer specifik signatur. Två saker tas dessutom **bort** utan att ersättas av något
229	nytt (`panel-open`, `panel-services`), vilket är iterationens signatur, inte nybyggets.
230	
231	### (5) Rörelsen
232	
233	**Motion-tes.**
234	
235	- **Focal:** ögat äger plåtens mittlinje. Vändningen sker runt plåtens egen vertikala
236	  mittaxel, så det som rör sig är exakt det som redan var i fokus vid ps = 0.
237	- **Continuity:** rubriken och underraden står stilla genom hela akten. De är stagens
238	  ground och de är kontinuitetsankaret som gör att vändningen läses som att *kortet*
239	  vänds och inte som att sidan byter scen.
240	- **Feedback:** varje scrollhack flyttar `--flip` med en lerpad andel, så handen får
241	  omedelbart svar; vid 90 grader syns bara hårlinjen, vilket är det ärliga svaret på
242	  "var är kortet nu".
243	- **Budget:** en pinnad akt på hela sidan, span 2,2 + dwell 0,35. Ingen annan akt får
244	  `pin`. Sidans övriga sex skärmar är `flow` med korta stagger.
245	
246	**Feeling curve** (en känsla per akt, aldrig två lika i rad):
247	
248	| Akt | Känsla | Vad på skärmen orsakar den |
249	|---|---|---|
250	| s1 hero, ps 0 till 0,12 | Igenkänning | Ett visitkort ligger stilla på ett bord i ett mörkt rum; ljuspölen vandrar långsamt över det |
251	| s2 hero, ps 0,12 till 0,72 | Nyfikenhet | Kortet börjar vändas av sig självt i takt med handen; vid 90 grader finns bara en hårlinje kvar |
252	| s3 hero, ps 0,72 till 1 | Erkännande | Baksidan landar och det är Alunix eget kort: namnet, vad de gör, och en väg in |
253	| s4 tes | Övertygelse | Ett helt materialbyte till blått, med Hyperborea-plåten som bryter sin egen kant |
254	| s5 bevis | Tillit | En riktig sajt laddar och går att titta på, inte en skärmbild |
255	| s6 pris | Lättnad | Tre priser står utskrivna utan att man behöver fråga |
256	| s7 avslut | Beslut | En rad, en adress, ingenting mer att göra |
257	
258	**Tell-someone-meningen:** *"Det är sidan där byråns visitkort ligger på bordet och vänds
259	när man scrollar, och baksidan är deras riktiga kort."*
260	
261	**Delight-tes, en mening:** kortet vänds.
262	
263	**Device-tabell** (>= 4 familjer, aldrig samma två i rad):
264	
265	| # | Akt | Device | Familj | Läser | Varför |
266	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
267	| 1 | s1-s3 hero | `pin` span 2.2 dwell 0.35 + bespoke `rotateY` på `.plate-card` | pin | **`--sc-ps`** | Vändningen är sidans topp och måste få mest scrollrum (`feel-and-fingerprint.md` § The peak) |
268	| 2 | s1 hero, inuti akten | bespoke `paintHeroPool` (`object-position` på `#heroPoolImg`) | bespoke paint | **`--sc-ps`** | `object-position` är något ögat ser förflytta sig, alltså F-014 punkt 1 |
269	| 3 | s4 tes | `drift` mot `#123f68` + `reveal="up"` på tesrubriken | drift | `--sc-p` för drift-tonen (ingen förflyttning), **`--sc-ps`** för Hyperborea-plåtens bleed-transform | Materialbytet är en ton, inte en rörelse; bleeden är en rörelse |
270	| 4 | s5 liggaren | bespoke ordscrub + självritande tråd | bespoke paint | **`--sc-ps`** | Orden och trådens `scaleY` förflyttar sig; F-014 punkt 1 |
271	| 5 | s5 Calyx | `reveal="up"` en gång, sedan ramen orörd | reveal | `--sc-p` (bara cue-opacitet) | En iframe får aldrig transformeras eller tonas efter att den visats (M1:s egen lärdom) |
272	| 6 | s6 Hōrai | `reveal="iris"` en gång | reveal (iris) | `--sc-p` (bara cue-opacitet) | Samma regel; iris öppnar ramen, rör den inte sedan |
273	| 7 | s6 jätterubriken | ren CSS `scale(0.92 -> 1)` | kinetic type | **`--sc-ps`** | Skalan är en transform; V3b läste `--sc-p` här och det är en av felen V3c rättar |
274	| 8 | s1-s7 grunden | `drift` i tre stopp | drift | `--sc-p` | Grunden byter ton, den förflyttar sig inte |
275	
276	Åtta poster, sex familjer (pin, bespoke paint, drift, reveal, iris-reveal, kinetic type),
277	aldrig samma två i rad.
278	
279	**`will-change`:** sätts på `.plate-card` (elementet som roterar, inte akt-behållaren)
280	enbart medan `0 < ps < 1`, tas bort i vila. `.giant`:s permanenta `will-change` **tas
281	bort**; det är en av de fyra vilande promoveringarna F-013 mätte.
282	
283	**Rejected-lista** (find-animation-opportunities-gaten; fyra frågor per kandidat:
284	frekvens, syfte, hastighet, funktion):
285	
286	| Kandidat | Frekvens | Syfte | Hastighet | Funktion | Dom |
287	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
288	| Kortet vänder sig också vid hover | Varje gång pekaren passerar plåten, alltså många gånger per besök | Inget; vändningen har redan hänt i akten | Skulle behöva vara snabb för att inte kännas trög, vilket motsäger aktens tempo | Ingen; den tar bort aktens engångskänsla | **Avvisad** |
289	| Ljuspölen följer pekaren (`--sc-mx`) | Kontinuerligt medan pekaren är i heron | Närvaro | Omedelbar | Ingen; den konkurrerar med scrollens egen koreografi om samma element | **Avvisad.** `feel-and-fingerprint.md`: "Embodiment is seasoning. One or two per page", och akten är redan sidans en |
290	| Liggarraderna lyfter vid hover | En gång per rad, ofta | Att visa att raden är interaktiv | 150 ms | Fel; raderna är inte länkar | **Avvisad** |
291	| Prisraderna räknar upp till sitt tal | En gång | "Dynamik" | 800 ms | Ingen; talen är fasta priser och en uppräkning gör dem svårare att läsa | **Avvisad.** TASTE § 4.9: siffror får vara textur bara som form, aldrig som föreställning |
292	| Hårlinjerna ritar sig in vid scroll | Sju gånger, en per skärm | Struktur | 300 ms | Marginell; strukturen finns redan i vila | **Avvisad.** Rörelse bara där typ och bild är tysta (TASTE § 4.8), och hårlinjerna sitter överallt |
293	| Kortet får en specular-hårlinje på den ledande kanten under vändningen | En gång, inuti akten | Att göra rotationsriktningen läsbar | Följer `--flip`, ingen egen tid | **Bärande.** Se § 7 och `runs/V3c/assets/ASSETS.md`: det är den ena rörelse som kompenserar för att stillbilden inte bär flippen | **Behållen** |
294	| Framsidan mörknar när planet vrider sig bort från ljuset | En gång, inuti akten | Fysisk trovärdighet | Följer `--flip` | **Bärande**, samma skäl | **Behållen** |
295	
296	### (6) Färgstrategi
297	
298	**Nivå: Restrained.** Sidan är en kontinuerlig svartvit fotografisk grund plus papper, och
299	exakt en kromatisk färg som gör exakt en sak.
300	
301	**Den fysiska scenen, i en mening:** ett mörkt rum där ett enda visitkort ligger på ett
302	bord under en snedställd lampa, och där ljuset längre in i sidan faller på en pappersark
303	i stället.
304	
305	**Låset, utskrivet, inget nytt val görs:** målbilden låser paletten till `#0b0c0e`
306	(grunden), `#fdfbf4` (papperet, R6-världen), `#1e5e9c` (accenten) och typsnitten till
307	**Geist** (röst: kortbaksidans ordmärke, liggarrubrikerna, den typsatta länken; Geist Mono
308	enbart som register, max fyra monoetiketter på sidan) och **Public Sans** (hero-rubriken i
309	vikt 300, jätterubriken, brödtext). Rollerna korsar aldrig. Ingen tredje familj.
310	Font-proceduren i `brand.md` körs inte om: valet är ärvt från en godkänd cell och att
311	öppna det vore ett nytt bygge, inte en iteration.
312	
313	**Accentens frekvenstal, skrivet som ett tal och inte som en känsla** (lånat från
314	`dope-security`): `#1e5e9c` förekommer **två** gånger på sidan: tesplåtens grund
315	(`data-sc-drift="#123f68"` är dess mörkare drift-mål, samma roll) och understrykningen i
316	`Boka ett möte ->` på kortbaksidan. Ingen tredje förekomst. Aldrig som ram, aldrig som
317	knappfyllning, aldrig i liggaren.
318	
319	### (7) Vad referenserna gör som cellen måste slå
320	
321	| Referens | Vad den gör | Vad V3c måste göra för att slå den |
322	|---|---|---|
323	| `garden-eight` (målbildens ribba, planens § 7.5) | Ett typografiskt moment och ett skulpturalt moment, åtskilda av tystnad, och ingenting annat ovanför vecket | V3c:s hero innehåller **exakt tre** element: rubrik, kort, en underrad. Ingen kicker, ingen cue, ingen tidsstämpel, ingen andra CTA. Mätbart: `preflight_taste.py` hero-regeln, textelement <= 4 |
324	| `mattis-studio` (låst av `select.py` OCH av V3b) | Konsolkortet med hörnmarkeringar är **platt**; det är en ritad ram runt typ | V3c:s kort är ett **fysiskt** kort som vänds: det har en baksida, en tjocklek läst ur hårlinjen vid 90 grader, och en ljuskälla som svarar på vinkeln. Mätbart: vid ps = 0,5 syns hårlinjen och ingenting annat av kortet |
325	| `squarespace` (målbildens ribba, planens § 7.5) | Svarta och vita band som byter genom skala, inte genom färg, med ett statistikblock och noll accent | V3c:s inversioner ska vara lika rena och göras **utan ett enda kort**: materialbytet sker i spalten själv (blått block, papper, mörkt prisblock), och det enda "statistikblocket" är tre sanna priser |
326	| `oryzo-ai` (topprankad av `select.py`) | Ett fysiskt objekt vrider sig i ett tomt mörkt rum, och det som gör rotationen läsbar är materialet och kanten under ett snedljus | V3c:s kort får inte vara två svarta rektangler som byter plats. Framsidan måste bära **material över hela ytan** och en ljusrespons som ändras med vinkeln. Detta är exakt fyndet i F-007-kontrollen nedan |
327	| `dope-security` | Anger accentens frekvens som ett tal och kapar skugga till en hårlinje | V3c skriver ut sitt eget accenttal (två förekomster) i decision ledger och har noll `box-shadow` |
328	| `monologue` | Håller sidans marginaler synliga med ett hårlinjeraster | V3c:s hårlinjer ligger på `--rail-x`-rastret, samma rutnät som rubriken och plåten, inte på egna värden |
329	| `planhat` (wildcard) | Vikt 300 i stor grad ligger alltid i fotots mörka parti | V3c:s rubrik ligger på den mörka grunden utanför plåten, aldrig över ljuspölen. Mätbart: `contrast_over_media.py --url` per grund |
330	
331	### (8) Rut-testet
332	
333	**Kategorins default för "digital byrå", i tre rader**, hållen utanför:
334	
335	1. Centrerad hero med en badge över rubriken, en fylld primärknapp och en spökknapp
336	   bredvid, ovanpå en mörk gradient eller ett suddigt kontorsfoto.
337	2. En logotypvägg med kundmärken, tre lika tjänstekort med ikoner, och en sifferrad med
338	   "200+ projekt / 15 år / 98 % nöjda kunder".
339	3. Ett citat med porträtt och ett kontaktformulär i botten, plus en sticky knapp som följer
340	   med hela vägen.
341	
342	Var målbilden möter defaulten, och vad som ändras:
343	
344	| Punkt där målbilden riskerar defaulten | Vad som ändras |
345	|---|---|
346	| **Tre tjänster.** Byråer räknar alltid upp tre tjänster; V3b gjorde det två gånger (liggaren och `panel-services`) | `panel-services` **tas bort**. Kvar är liggaren, som är rader med siffror på papper, inte kort med ikoner. Och tjänsteorden repeteras en tredje gång på kortbaksidan, men i **monoregister på 10,5 px**, alltså som en signatur och inte som en tjänstelista |
347	| **En CTA i heron.** Defaulten sätter "Boka ett möte" som en fylld knapp direkt under rubriken | `Boka ett möte ->` finns bara på **kortets baksida**, alltså först efter att besökaren scrollat genom hela akten, och den är en **typsatt länk** med understrykning i accenten, inte en knapp. Ingen sticky CTA finns |
348	| **Ordmärket i heron.** Defaulten sätter loggan uppe till vänster i en navrad | Ordmärket finns två gånger: i den tunna toppraden som scrollar bort, och i affischgrad på kortets baksida. Den andra förekomsten är hela akten's poäng, inte chrome |
349	| **Sifferraden.** Defaulten fyller ut med tal | V3c har **noll** tal utom de tre priserna, som är sanna. TASTE § 4.9 tillåter formen bara med sant innehåll |
350	| **Kontaktformuläret** | Ersatt av `kontakt@alunix.se` som en textrad och en mailto. Inget formulär, inget fält, ingen skickaknapp |
351	| **Mörk gradient som grund** | Ersatt av ett kontinuerligt fotografi i gråskala som tonas via `--sc-canvas`-drift. Materialet är en riktig yta, inte en färgövergång |
352	
353	---
354	
355	## F-007-kontrollen av hero-plattans nuvarande stillbild
356	
357	Läst som pixlar: `tests/alunix-concepts-r3/build/assets/k1-stage-pool.webp` (1600x1067,
358	65 kB) och den byggda folden `tests/alunix-concepts-r5/cells/V3b-chain/shots/desktop-1440--fold.png`.
359	
360	**Dom: nej, ljuspölen bär inte flippen.** Tre mätbara skäl, i fallande materialitet:
361	
362	1. **Fram- och baksida delar värde.** Cirka 60 % av bildens yta (hela övre bandet och
363	   högra tredjedelen) ligger på eller nära ren svart, och baksidan är
364	   `background: var(--c-black)`. Vändningen går alltså från "svart rektangel" till
365	   "svart rektangel med text". Det ögat ska läsa som två sidor av ett kort läser som
366	   samma sida två gånger.
367	2. **Ingen kant och ingen struktur att förkorta.** Motivet är en mjuk, kantlös ellips av
368	   ljus på tyg. En Y-rotation blir läsbar genom att raka linjer och kanter förkortas i
369	   perspektiv; en gradientfläck har inga. `oryzo-ai`:s skivor 02 och 08 visar motsatsen
370	   mätt: där bär korkens kant och spräckliga material hela rotationen.
371	3. **Logo-docken sitter på död svart.** I den byggda folden ligger ordmärket i plåtens
372	   övre vänstra hörn, på ett parti utan textur. Framsidan har alltså inget material där
373	   ögat landar först.
374	
375	**Ingen omtagning beställs.** Higgsfield har 0 krediter (free plan, mätt av lead
376	2026-09-09), så generering är ute; se `runs/V3c/assets/ASSETS.md` för de kvarvarande
377	vägarna i planens § 10.6 steg 3-ordning och den rekommenderade vägen, och
378	`runs/V3c/BRIEF.md` § decision ledger för raden som skriver in bytet.

# Alunix r8, målbild V3c (arkitektens del)

Denna fil äger **bara** cell V3c. Lead slår ihop V3c, K3 och K4 till `concepts.md`.
Källa: planens § 7.5, ordagrant speglad i `tests/alunix-r8/malbilder/V3c.md`, som är
bindande. Varje avvikelse nedan har en rad i `runs/V3c/BRIEF.md` § decision ledger med
källa.

---

## § sweep_raw

```
$ python scripts/catalogue/sweep_raw.py
sweep: rent - varje kalla under raw/ och processed/ har en post (0 ignorerade).
EXIT=0
```

Kört av arkitekten 2026-09-09, bekräftar leads körning. Grinden är öppen.

## § catalogue-select

Brieffilen: `tests/alunix-r8/runs/V3c/BRIEF-draft.md` (arkitektens utkast, skrivet enbart
för att skriptet ska ha deklarerade fält att poängsätta mot; den är inte cellens brief).

```
$ python scripts/catalogue/select.py --brief tests/alunix-r8/runs/V3c/BRIEF-draft.md --k 4 --wildcard --explain
Brief: tests\alunix-r8\runs\V3c\BRIEF-draft.md  ->  5 poster

   14  oryzo-ai                 cinematic dark         continuous world
       +3 register | +3 grammatik | +2 category2 | +6 fritext (accent, black, button, display)
   12  dope-security            cinematic dark         split stage
       +3 register | +2 category | +1 mode | +6 fritext (accent, button, glass, hairline)
   12  mattis-studio            cinematic dark         split stage
       +3 register | +2 category | +1 mode | +6 fritext (agency, beside, black, display)
   12  monologue                cinematic dark         split stage
       +3 register | +2 category | +1 mode | +6 fritext (colour, display, headline, mono)
   12  planhat                  cinematic dark         split stage
       +3 register | +2 category | +1 mode | +6 fritext (cards, cinematic, dark, display) | wildcard: utanfor kategorin

Mediastrategi ur posternas egna falt (Photo search) - locken ska inte gissa:
  - oryzo-ai: Unsplash first, Pexels second. - "craft tools top down workbench flat lay" - "cutting mat pencil knife top down" - "product design workshop
  - dope-security: Unsplash first, Pexels second. - "dramatic twilight sky purple clouds horizon" - "dusk sky gradient clouds wide format" - "airplane light tr
  - mattis-studio: Unsplash first, Pexels second. - "black and white fashion editorial studio" - "monochrome portrait high contrast studio" - "editorial fashio
  - monologue: Unsplash first, Pexels second. - "dark texture ripple abstract background" - "black fabric wave texture close up" - "dark water surface ripp
  - planhat: Unsplash first, Pexels second. - "misty forest golden hour light" - "sunlight through trees atmospheric" - "moody forest landscape warm tone

catalogue-select skriven: oryzo-ai, dope-security, mattis-studio, monologue, planhat  ->  C:\Users\Anton L\anti-slop-design\.impeccable\design-session.jsonl
```

**Låst rad:** `catalogue-select: oryzo-ai, dope-security, mattis-studio, monologue, planhat`
(`--k 4 --wildcard`, wildcard = `planhat`).

**Urvalet motsäger planens gissning, och skriptet vinner.** Planens § 7.5 skrev
"förväntat: `garden-eight`, `mattis-studio`, `squarespace`, ev. `creative-giants`" men
säger samtidigt att referenserna "låses via `select.py`". Bara `mattis-studio` överlappar.
Orsaken är mekanisk och kontrollerad: `garden-eight` och `creative-giants` står som
`editorial print` / `typographic poster` och `squarespace` som `modern clean` /
`chaptered editorial` i `index.json`, medan V3c ärver V3b:s värld, som är `cinematic dark`
/ `continuous world`. Gissningen beskrev vad V3c ska **slå**, inte vilken värld den bor i.

Konsekvens, skriven som beslut och inte som tyst avvikelse:

- **Låset (`reference-lock.md` Tier 0, "Primary = the locked system itself"):** primär
  riktning är V3b själv, `tests/alunix-concepts-r5/cells/V3b-chain/index.html`. V3c är en
  iteration; det är den enda ärliga primärkällan.
- **Lånade detaljer (max två, per `reference-lock.md`):** `oryzo-ai`:s fysiska objekt som
  vrider sig i ett mörkt tomrum, och `mattis-studio`:s konsolram, som lånas **som
  avvisning** (V3c:s kort är ett fysiskt kort, inte en platt ram).
- **`garden-eight` och `squarespace` behåller sina rader i § 7 som ribbor** eftersom
  målbilden namnger dem, med källan utskriven: planens § 7.5, inte `select.py`.
  `creative-giants` faller helt; ingen källa stödjer den.

## § Lästa referenser

Tre rader per fil: vad den gör, vad jag tar, vad jag lämnar. Bilder lästa som pixlar med
`Read`, text som text.

### oryzo-ai (topprankad; samma register OCH samma grammatik som V3c)

| Fil | Gör | Tar | Lämnar |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fold.webp` | Ovanifrån-foto av korkunderlägget på skärbräda, ordmärke i affischgrad uppe till vänster, halvtransparent creditkort nere till vänster, "SCROLL TO CONTINUE" i botten | Ordmärke i affischgrad som får dela fold med ett objekt utan att konkurrera, därför att objektet ligger i en annan ljushet | Scroll-cuen (gate 88), creditkortet som lager över fotot, den varma paletten |
| `slices/02.webp` | Objektet lutar i ett mörkt tomrum, rubriken i två rader vänster, brödtext höger, inget annat | **Kärnlärdomen för V3c:** ett fysiskt objekt läses som roterande därför att dess *material och kant* fångar ett snedljus, inte därför att rotationen finns | Den varma walnut-grunden, versal-500-rösten, tre textkolumner runt objektet |
| `slices/04.webp` | Samma objekt hålls i en hand, rubriken "Powered by AI" i display, orange kredit under | Att objektet får en enda ljuskälla och att bakgrunden är helt tom runt det | Händer (förbjudet på Alunix, `generation.md` § Never), orange, "AI"-tonläget |
| `slices/06.webp` | Regnbågsram runt hela viewporten vid hover-läge, samma objekt | Ingenting | Hela greppet: en kromatisk ram runt viewporten är gate 89-territorium och bryter "ett papper, en accent" |

## V3c · Plåt i grunden · kortet vänds

### (1) Auktoritet och vad som viker

**Auktoriteten är typen** (TASTE § 1, raden "Typen (ordmärke eller rubrik i
viewport-bredd)"): rubriken `Er hemsida är nutidens visitkort` i affischgrad utanför
plåten bär sidan, och den står kvar genom hela den pinnade akten som stagens ground.

Vad som viker, en mening var: **fotot** viker genom att stanna lågexponerat inuti plåten
och aldrig gå fullbleed. **Ytan** viker genom att vara en enda kontinuerlig svartvit grund
utan sektionsfärger, så materialbytet sker i spalterna och inte i grunden. **Färgen**
viker genom att `#1e5e9c` bara gör en sak, den blå tesplåten, och aldrig blir knapp,
ram eller understryk. **Rörelsen** viker på hela sidan **utom i signaturakten**, där
TASTE § 4.8:s r6-precisering gäller: i set-piecet är rörelsen auktoriteten, och där är
typen redan vikt 300 och fotot redan lågexponerat.

**Mätningen som gör "ett displayelement" sant genom hela akten:** vid 1440 är plåten
`min(1440 - 2*rail, 56vh*16/9)` = 896 px bred, och kortbaksidans `ALUNIX` klampar på
`9cqw` av plåtens egen container = 81 px (taket `7.5rem` = 120 px binder inte).
Hero-rubriken ligger på ~9cqw av sidans container = ~130 px. Kvoten är 0,62, alltså det
"ett steg ner" TASTE § 1 kräver, och 81 px mot 16 px brödtext är 5,1x, alltså över
TASTE § 2.4:s golv. **Byggaren mäter och rapporterar båda talen vid 1440; målvärde
kvot <= 0,70 och baksidans display >= 5x brödtexten.**
